<!-- theorem-1: body_md -->
\label{thm_UML}
    There exists a constant $c(g+t,d)$ satisfying the property as follows. Let $\Gamma\subset G(K)$ be a subgroup of finite rank. Let $X\subset G$ be a closed subvariety with $d={\mathrm{deg}}_{L+M}(\overline X)$. Then there are at most $c(g+t,d)^{\mathrm{rk}(\Gamma)+1}$ cosets $H_1,H_2,\dots$ contained in $X$ such that
$$X(K)\cap\Gamma=\bigcup H_i(K)\cap\Gamma.$$
<!-- end theorem-1 -->
<!-- theorem-2: body_md -->
\label{thm_UML_pts}
There exists a constant $c'(g+t,d)$ satisfying the property as follows. Let $G,X$ and $\Gamma$ be as in Theorem \ref{thm_UML}. Then
$$\#(X^\circ(\overline\mathbb{Q})\cap\Gamma)\le c'(g+t,d)^{\mathrm{rk}(\Gamma)+1}.$$
<!-- end theorem-2 -->
<!-- theorem-3: body_md -->
\label{SUBC}
There exists a positive constant $c_3=c_3(g+t,d)>0$ satisfying the property as follows. Let $G,L$ and $X$ be as in Theorem \ref{thm_UML}, with $L$ being a pull-back of a principal polarization on $A$. Assume $X$ generates $A$, and $X$ has finite stabilizer. Then there exists a reduced subscheme $Z\subsetneq X$ of degree $${\mathrm{deg}} Z\le c_1(g+t,d),$$ and a point $g_0\in G(\overline{\mathbb Q})$ such that for any $g_1\in G(\overline{\mathbb Q})$, we have
$$\{x\in X^\circ(\overline\mathbb{Q}):\widehat{h}(x-g_1)\le c_3(g+t,d)\widehat h(g_1-g_0)\}\subset Z(\overline\mathbb{Q}).$$
Here $c_1(g+t,d)$ is the constant in Theorem \ref{bogomolov}.
<!-- end theorem-3 -->
<!-- remark-1: body_md -->
Let us clarify some terminologies.

Classically, the \emph{uniform Bogomolov conjecture} is  the height inequality in Theorem \ref{SUBC} by $\widehat h(x)\leq c_3'(g+t,d)$ for some other constant $c_3'$. 
In the abelian case, this is precisely \cite[Theorem 1.3]{GGK}. Before their result, \cite{DP07Minoration,DKY2020genus2,Kuhne} proved some cases. Notice that this version cannot imply uniform Mordell--Lang, even for curves; see \cite[below Theorem~1.3]{GGK}. Indeed, to achieve uniform Mordell--Lang, one needs a stronger version of {\it uniform Bogomolov}, called the {\it new gap principle} in \cite[Theorem~4.1]{ZG_Survey} and \cite[Theorem 1.2]{GGK}. Yuan's \cite[Theorem 1.1]{Yuan2026bigness} further strengthens this uniform Bogomolov type result by introducing an extra term.

During the preparation of the current article, we were told by Hultberg that using the GVF theory \cite{yaacov2022GVF}, a generalization of \cite[Theorem 1.2, Theorem 1.3]{GGK} to semiabelian varieties has been proven \cite{hultberg2026newgap} with a stronger condition that $X$ generates $G$. The key to the proof is a reduction to Gao--Ge--Kühne \cite{GGK} via the relative Faltings-Zhang method established by Luo--Yu \cite{luo2025gbc} on geometric Bogomolov conjecture for semiabelian varieties.

However, in our case, the direct generalization of \cite[Theorem 1.2]{GGK} to semiabelian varieties can {\bf not} deduce Theorem~\ref{thm_UML} due to the absence of Mumford's inequality. The version with the extra term is hence necessary.
<!-- end remark-1 -->
<!-- theorem-4: body_md -->
Let $\overline\eta$ be the geometric generic point of $S$.
    Assume that 
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item For every $s\in S$, $\mathcal X_s$  generates $(\mathcal A_g)_s$;
        \item $\mathcal X_{\overline \eta}$ is irreducible and has finite stabilizer.
    \end{enumerate}
    Then $\mathcal X^{[m]}:=\underbrace{\mathcal X\times_S\cdots\times_S\mathcal X}_{m\text{ times}}$ is non-degenerate for every $m\gg 0.$
<!-- end theorem-4 -->
<!-- theorem-5: body_md -->
Assume that the abelian quotient of $\mathcal G$ is principally polarized, and $\mathcal X$ is non-degenerate.
Let $x_i\in{\mathcal X}\ (n=1,2\dots)$ be a generic sequence of algebraic points. If
$$\lim_{i\to\infty}\widehat{h}(x_i)=0,$$
then the average Galois orbit of the sequence $(x_i)$ equidistributes to
a probability measure $\mu$ on $\mathcal X(\mathbb{C}).$
<!-- end theorem-5 -->
<!-- lemma-1: body_md -->
\label{lemm_normality_weight-2}
    Any $\mathbb{Q}$-vector subgroup of $\mathrm M_{t,1}$ is normal in $P_{g,t}.$
<!-- end lemma-1 -->
<!-- proof-1: body_md -->
This this a direct consequence of the matrix representation of $P_{g,t}.$
<!-- end proof-1 -->
<!-- remark-2: body_md -->
Here we add an explanation of the bijection in \eqref{eq_betti_matrix}. For any $\upsilon\in \mathcal X_{g,t}^+$, there exists $(z,y,x,h)\in P_{g,t}^{\mathrm{der}}(\mathbb{R})^+\mathrm M_{t,1}(\mathbb{C})$ such that $(z,y,x,h)\cdot (0,0,0,\tau_0)=\upsilon$, and for any other such $(z',y',x',h')$, we have $(z,y,x)=(z',y',x').$ 
    This is the special case of the general argument in \cite[(4.1)]{ZGAxLindemann}.
<!-- end remark-2 -->
<!-- remark-3: body_md -->
Our formula for $\widetilde b_\mathrm{ab}$ is slightly different with \cite{ZG1} since we use the real coordinate $v=y_1-\tau y_2$ instead of $v=y_1+\tau y_2$.
<!-- end remark-3 -->
<!-- proposition-1: body_md -->
\label{prop_betti_equivariant}
The universal Betti map $\widetilde b$ is $P_{g,t}(\mathbb{R})^+\mathrm{M}_{t,1}(\mathbb{C})$-equivariant in the sense that for any $q=(z,y,x,h)\in (\mathrm{M}_{t,1}(\mathbb{C})\oplus \mathrm M_{2g,1}(\mathbb{R}))\rtimes \mathrm{M}_{t,2g}(\mathbb{R})\rtimes \mathrm{GSp}_{2g}(\mathbb{R})^+=P_{g,t}(\mathbb{R})^+\mathrm{M}_{t,1}(\mathbb{C})$, and $\upsilon\in \mathcal X_{g,t}^+$,
\[{ \begin{aligned} \widetilde{b}_{\mathrm{ab}}(q\cdot\upsilon) &= h \widetilde{b}_{\mathrm{ab}}(\upsilon)+y, \\ \widetilde{b}_{\mathrm{tor}}(q\cdot\upsilon) &= \mu(h) \, \widetilde{b}_{\mathrm{tor}}(\upsilon)+x \widetilde{b}_{\mathrm{ab}}(\upsilon) + z.  \end{aligned}}\]
In particular, the map $\mathbb{C}^t\times \mathbb{R}^{2g}\rightarrow \mathbb{C}^t\times \mathbb{R}^{2g}, \widetilde b(\upsilon)\mapsto \widetilde b(q\cdot \upsilon)$ is a diffeomorphism.
<!-- end proposition-1 -->
<!-- proof-2: body_md -->
The formula follows from direct matrix multiplication computation via \eqref{eq_betti_matrix}. We may also refer to \cite[pp. 15]{ZGAxLindemann} for a general discussion. Therefore for any $q$, the map $\widetilde b(\upsilon)\mapsto \widetilde b(q\cdot\upsilon)$ is differentiable. As it has the obvious inverse $\widetilde b(\upsilon)\mapsto \widetilde b(q^{-1}\cdot\upsilon)$ which is also differentiable, we conclude the proof.
<!-- end proof-2 -->
<!-- proposition-2: body_md -->
\cite[Proposition 2.9]{ZGAxLindemann}\label{prop_weight_decomp}
    Let $f:(P,\mathcal X^+)\rightarrow (P',\mathcal X‘^+)$ be a Shimura morphism of connected mixed Shimura data. Then
    $$f(U)\subset U'\quad\text{and}\quad f(\mathcal R_u(P))\subset \mathcal R_u(P'),$$
    where $U'$ is the normal subgroup of $P'$ of weight $-2$ part.
<!-- end proposition-2 -->
<!-- theorem-6: body_md -->
\label{theorem_special_subvariety}
    Assume that \begin{equation}\label{eq_split_unipotent_radical}
        V^{\mathrm{ab}}_Q=V_Q,\text{ i.e., } \mathcal R_u(p_{\pi}(Q))=V^{\mathrm{ab}}_Q\oplus W_Q.
    \end{equation}
    Then $M\rightarrow \pi_{\mathrm{sab}}(M)$ is a torsion translation of semiabelian subscheme of $\mathcal P_{g,t}^\times|_{\pi_{\mathrm{sab}}(M)}.$
<!-- end theorem-6 -->
<!-- lemma-2: body_md -->
\label{lemm_split_unipotnent_radical}
    The condition \eqref{eq_split_unipotent_radical}, is equivalent to $$\pi(M)=\pi_{\mathrm{ab}}(M)\times_{\pi_{\mathrm{Siegel}}(M)}\pi_{\mathrm{sab}}(M).$$
<!-- end lemma-2 -->
<!-- proof-3: body_md -->
Consider the quotient $\mathcal A_1:=(\mathcal A_g|_{\pi_{\mathrm{Siegel}}(M)})\times_{\pi_{\mathrm{Siegel}}(M)}{\pi_{\mathrm{sab}}(M)}\rightarrow \mathcal A_2:=\mathcal A_g|_{\pi_{\mathrm{Siegel}}(M)}$, which is a Shimura quotient given by the data:
    \begin{align*}
        &((\mathrm M_{2g,1}\oplus W_Q)\rtimes G_Q, (p_{\pi}(q_0)+\mathrm M_{2g,1}(\mathbb{R})\oplus W_Q(\mathbb{R}))\times \widetilde\pi_{\mathrm{Siegel}}(M))\\&\kern 12em\longrightarrow (\mathrm M_{2g,1}\rtimes G_Q, (p_{\mathrm{ab}}(q_0)+\mathrm M_{2g,1}(\mathbb{R}))\times \widetilde\pi_{\mathrm{Siegel}}(M))
    \end{align*}
    where the section $G_Q\rightarrow (\mathrm M_{2g,1}\oplus W_Q)\rtimes G_Q$ is a conjugation by $p_{\pi}(q_0).$ Then $\pi(M)\subset \mathcal A_1$ is the preimage of $\pi_{\mathrm{ab}}(M)\subset \mathcal A_2$ by condition \eqref{eq_split_unipotent_radical}.

    Conversely, since $\pi(M)$ is a connected mixed Shimura subvariety of $\mathcal A_g\times_{\mathbb A_g} (\mathcal A_g^{\vee})^{[t]},$ associated with the Shimura subdatum $(p_{\pi}(Q),\widetilde \pi(\mathcal Y^+)),$ by \cite[Propoosition 3.4 and its proof]{ZG2017}, we have that
    \begin{itemize}
                                                                                                                                                          
                                                                                                                                   
        \item The group $p_{\pi}(Q)$ is the conjugate of $(V_Q\oplus W_Q)\rtimes G_Q < (\mathrm M_{2g,1}\oplus \mathrm M_{t,2g})\rtimes \mathrm{GSp}_{2g}$ by $(p_{\pi}(q_0),1);$
        \item Via the semi-algebraic identification \eqref{eq_betti_matrix},
        $$\widetilde \pi(\mathcal Y^+)=(p_{\pi}(q_0)+V_Q(\mathbb{R})\oplus W_Q(\mathbb{R}))\times \widetilde \pi_{\mathrm{Siegel}}(\mathcal Y^+).$$
    \end{itemize}
    Similarly, we have $\widetilde\pi_{\mathrm{sab}}(\mathcal Y^+)=(p_{\mathrm{sab}}(q_0)+W_Q(\mathbb{R}))\times \widetilde \pi_{\mathrm{Siegel}}(\mathcal Y^+).$
    By the condition \eqref{eq_split_unipotent_radical}, we see  
    that $\pi(M)=\pi_{\mathrm{ab}}(M)\times_{\pi_{\mathrm {Siegel}}(M)}\pi_{\mathrm{sab}}(M).$
<!-- end proof-3 -->
<!-- lemma-3: body_md -->
\label{lemma_abelian_section}
    Let $S$ be a projective variety over an algebraically closed field $k$. 
    Let $0\rightarrow \mathbb G_{m,S}^t\rightarrow \mathcal G\rightarrow \mathcal A\rightarrow 0$ be a semiabelian scheme. Assume that we have a section $\sigma: \mathcal A\rightarrow \mathcal G$ of $\mathcal A$. Then $\mathcal G=\mathcal A\times \mathbb G_m^t$ and $\sigma (\mathcal A)=\mathcal A\times\{x\}$ for some $x\in \mathbb G_m^t$.
<!-- end lemma-3 -->
<!-- proof-4: body_md -->
Consider \begin{align*}
        h:\mathcal A^{[2]}=\mathcal A\times_S\mathcal A&\longrightarrow \mathbb G_m^t\\
        (a,b)&\longmapsto \sigma(a+b)\sigma (a)^{-1}\sigma(b)^{-1}
    \end{align*}
    Since $\mathcal A^{[2]}$ is projective, $h$ has to be a constant map. We set $x\in \mathbb G_m^t$ to be the image.

    After replacing $\sigma$ with its translation by the section $\{-x\}\times S\subset \mathbb G_m^t\times S\subset \mathcal G$, we may assume that $x=0.$ Then we see that $\sigma$ is a group homomorphism.

    We thus have the homomorphism $\mathcal G\rightarrow \mathcal A\times \mathbb G_m^t, g\mapsto (\pi(g),g\sigma(\pi(g))^{-1})$ which concludes the proof.
<!-- end proof-4 -->
<!-- proof-5: body_md -->
Put $P:=((\mathrm M_{t,1}\oplus V_Q)\rtimes W_Q)\rtimes G_Q$ and $\mathcal X^+:=\mathcal X_{g,t}^+|_{\widetilde \pi(M)}.$ Then $(P,\mathcal X^+)$ is the connected mixed Shimura datum of $M_P:=\mathcal P_{g,t}^\times |_{\pi(M)}.$ By Lemma \ref{lemm_split_unipotnent_radical}, $M_P$ is also a semiabelian $\pi_{\mathrm{sab}}(M)$-subscheme of $\mathcal P_{g,t}^\times|_{\pi_{\mathrm{sab}}(M)}$ up to a torsion translation.

    Let $t'=\dim U_Q$ and $\mathbb G_m^{t'}$ be the subtorus of $\mathbb G_m^t$ given by the saturation of the lattice $\mathbb{Z}^t\cap U_Q$. Since $U_Q$ is normal in $P$ by Lemma \ref{lemm_normality_weight-2},
    we have the commutative diagram of $\pi_{\mathrm{sab}}(M)$-schemes
    \[\begin{tikzcd}
	M_{/U_Q} & (M_P)_{/U_Q}=M_P/\mathbb G_m^{t'}\\
	 & {\pi(M)}
	\arrow[hook, from=1-1, to=1-2]
	\arrow["\mathrm{id}",from=1-1, to=2-2]
	\arrow[from=1-2, to=2-2]
\end{tikzcd}\]
    where $M_{/U_Q}$ (resp. $(M_P)_{/U_Q}$) is the Shimura quotient of $M$ (resp. $M_P$) by $U_Q$. Since $M$ is the preimage of $M_{/U_Q}$ in $M_P$, it suffices to prove that $M_{/U_Q}$ is a torsion translation of an abelian $\pi_{\mathrm{sab}}(M)$-subscheme of $(M_P)_{/U_Q}.$

    Applying Lemma \ref{lemma_abelian_section} to each fiber of $M_P/\mathbb G_m^{t'}$ over $\pi_{\mathrm{Siegel}}(M)$, we obtain that \begin{enumerate}
    \item[(i)] $M_P/\mathbb G_m^{t'}$ is isomorphic to $\pi(M)\times \mathbb G_m^{t-t'}$ as semiabelian schemes over $\pi_{\mathrm{sab}}(M)$,
    \item[(ii)] and the inclusion $M_{/U_Q}\hookrightarrow M_P/\mathbb G_m^{t'}$ is a translation of $\pi(M)$ by $\sigma$, where $\sigma:\pi_{\mathrm{Siegel}}(M)\rightarrow \mathbb G_m^{t-t'}$ is a morphism of varieties.
    \end{enumerate} 

    Now it suffices to prove that $\sigma$ is a constant map to a torsion point.

    Note that the Levi decomposition $P=\mathcal R_u(P)\rtimes G_Q$ gives that
    $$\mathcal X^+=(q_0+ U_P(\mathbb{C})\mathcal R_u(P)(\mathbb{R}))\times \widetilde\pi_{\mathrm{Siegel}}(M).$$ 
    
    By (i), we see that $V_Q\oplus W_Q$ is a normal subgroup of $P/U_P$, hence so is its preimage $\mathcal R_u(Q)$. After taking the quotient of $M_P$ and $M$ by $\mathcal R_u(Q)$, we obtain that 
    \begin{align*}
        \mathcal Y^+_{/\mathcal R_u(Q)}&=\{\widetilde q_0\}\times \widetilde \pi_{\mathrm{Siegel}}(M),\\
        \mathcal X^+_{/\mathcal R_u(Q)}&=(\widetilde q_0+ (U_P/U_Q)(\mathbb{C}))\times \widetilde\pi_{\mathrm{Siegel}}(M).
    \end{align*}
    Then $\sigma$ is exactly the map $$\pi_{\mathrm{Siegel}}(M)\simeq\mathbf{u}(\mathcal Y^+_{/\mathcal R_u(Q)})\rightarrow \mathbf{u}(\mathcal X^+_{/\mathcal R_u(Q)}).$$
    Therefore we conclude the proof using the fact that $q_0$ is a $\mathbb{Q}$-point.
<!-- end proof-5 -->
<!-- lemma-4: body_md -->
We have $N\cap (\mathrm{M}_{t,1}\oplus \mathrm M_{2g,1})=U_N\oplus V_N <\mathrm{M}_{t,1}\oplus \mathrm M_{2g,1}.$
<!-- end lemma-4 -->
<!-- proof-6: body_md -->
Let $V':=N\cap (\mathrm{M}_{t,1}\oplus \mathrm M_{2g,1}).$ For any $\widetilde y\in \mathcal Y^+,$ $\mathbf{u}(U_N(\mathbb{C})V'(\mathbb{R})\widetilde y)$ is a weakly special subvariety of $(\mathcal P_{g,t}^\times)_s$ for $s=\pi_{\mathrm{sab}}(\mathbf{u}(\widetilde y))$. By \cite[Proposition 7.2]{ZGAxLindemann}, $\mathbf{u}(U_N(\mathbb{C})V'(\mathbb{R})\widetilde y)$ is a translate of subgroups, hence $V'=U_N\oplus V_N.$
<!-- end proof-6 -->
<!-- proposition-3: body_md -->
\label{prop_normality_triviality} 
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item $U_N\oplus V^{\mathrm{ab}}_N$ is a normal subgroup of $Q$. Equivalently, it is a $p_{\mathrm{sab}}(Q)$-submodule of $U_Q\oplus V_Q.$
        \item $p_{\mathrm{sab}}(N)$ acts trivially on $(U_Q\oplus V_Q)/(U_N\oplus V^{\mathrm{ab}}_N).$
    \end{enumerate}
<!-- end proposition-3 -->
<!-- proof-7: body_md -->
(1) The Levi-decomposition $Q=R_Q\rtimes G_Q$ induces a Levi decomposition $W_Q\rtimes G_Q$ of $p_{\mathrm{sab}}(Q)$. 

    By \cite[Proposition 3.5]{ZG2017}, $V^{\mathrm{ab}}_N$ is $G_Q$-equivariant. By the representation of $P_{g,t}$, we have the following diagram 
    \[\begin{tikzcd}
	G_Q\times (U_Q\oplus V_Q)&G_Q\times U_Q & \\
	U_Q\oplus V_Q & U_Q
	\arrow["\mathrm{id}\times{\mathrm{pr}_{U_Q}}", from=1-1, to=1-2]
	\arrow[from=1-1, to=2-1]
    \arrow["{\mathrm{pr}_{U_Q}}",from=2-1, to=2-2]
	\arrow[from=1-2, to=2-2]
    \end{tikzcd}\]
    where the vertical arrows are group actions of $G_Q$.
    Hence $U_N\oplus V_N^{\mathrm{ab}}$ is $G_Q$-equivariant by the normality of $U_N$ due to Lemma \ref{lemm_normality_weight-2}.
    
    Now it suffices to prove that $U_N\oplus V^{\mathrm{ab}}_N$ is $W_Q$-equivariant, i.e., $U_N\oplus V^{\mathrm{ab}}_N$ is normal in $R_Q$.                                                                                                                                                                 
    Since the action of $W_Q$ on $V_Q$ is trivial, the action of $W_Q$ on $(U_Q\oplus V_Q)$ is given by $$x\cdot (z,y)\longmapsto (z+f_x(y),y)$$
    where $(x \in W_Q)\mapsto (f_x\in \mathrm{Hom}(V_Q,U_Q))$ is a group homomorphism.
    Hence it suffices to prove that $f_x(y)\in U_N$ for any $y\in V^{\mathrm{ab}}_N$ and $x\in W_Q$.

    Since $V^{\mathrm{ab}}_N=p_{\mathrm{ab}}(N)\cap \mathrm{M}_{2g,1}=p_{\mathrm{ab}}(N\cap \mathcal R_u(Q))$, there exists $n=(z_0,y,x_0)\in N\cap \mathcal R_u(Q)\subset (U_Q\oplus V^{\mathrm{ab}}_Q)\rtimes W_Q$ such that $p_{\mathrm{ab}}(n)=y.$
    Then $$(0,0,x)n(0,0,x)^{-1}=(z_0+f_x(y),y,x+x_0)\cdot (0,0,-x)=(z_0+f_x(y),y,x_0)$$
    which exactly gives that $f_x(y)\in U_N.$

    (2) Since $p_{\mathrm{ab}}(N)\trianglelefteq p_{\mathrm{ab}}(Q)$, $G_N$ acts trivially on $V_Q/V_N^\mathrm{ab}$. Similarly as in (1), by the representation of $P_{g,t}$, $G_N$ acts trivially on $(U_Q\oplus V_Q)/(U_N\oplus V_N^\mathrm{ab}).$
    
    Now it suffices to prove that $W_N$ acts trivially on $(U_Q\oplus V_Q)/(U_N\oplus V^{\mathrm{ab}}_N),$ i.e.,
    for any $x\in W_N$ and $(z',y')\in U_Q\oplus V_Q$, \begin{equation}\label{eq_poincare_pairing}
        x\cdot (z',y')-(z',y')\in U_N\oplus V^{\mathrm{ab}}_N\Leftrightarrow f_{x}(y')\in U_N.
    \end{equation}

    Since $W_N=p_{\mathrm{sab}}(\mathcal R_u(N))\subset (U_Q\oplus V_Q)\rtimes W_Q$, there exists an element $n=(z,y,x)\in \mathcal R_u(N)$. Let $q=(0,y',0)\in Q$. By the normality of $N$, the commutator
    \begin{align*}
        nq n^{-1}q^{-1}=(f_x(y'),y',0)q^{-1}=(f_x(y'),0,0)\in U_N,
    \end{align*}
    which concludes the proof.
<!-- end proof-7 -->
<!-- corollary-1: body_md -->
\label{coro_semiabelian_subscheme}
    Let $M_0:=\mathbf{u}(U_N(\mathbb{C})\times V^{\mathrm{ab}}_N(\mathbb{R})\times \widetilde\pi_{\mathrm{sab}}(\mathcal Y^+)).$ Then $M_0$ is a semiabelian $\pi_{\mathrm{sab}}(M)$-subscheme of $M$.
<!-- end corollary-1 -->
<!-- proof-8: body_md -->
Notice that $\pi(M_0)=\mathbf{u}(V^{\mathrm{ab}}_N(\mathbb{R})\times \widetilde \pi_{\mathrm{sab}}(\mathcal Y^+))$ is an abelian $\pi_{\mathrm{sab}}(M)$-subscheme of $\pi(M)$ by \cite[Rappels 4.4.3]{PD}.
    Then $M_R:=\pi|_M^{-1}(\pi(M_0))$ is a semiabelian $\pi_{\mathrm{sab}}(M)$-subscheme of $M$.
    
    Taking the Shimura quotient of $M$ by $U_N$, we obtain the following commutative diagram:
    \[\begin{tikzcd}
	\rho_{/U_N}(M_0)& \rho_{/U_N}(M_R) &M_{/U_N}\\
	 & \pi(M_0) & {\pi(M)}
	\arrow[hook, from=1-1, to=1-2]
    \arrow[hook, from=1-2, to=1-3]
	\arrow["\mathrm{id}",from=1-1, to=2-2]
	\arrow[from=1-2, to=2-2]
    \arrow[hook, from=2-2, to=2-3]
    \arrow[from=1-3, to=2-3]
\end{tikzcd}.\]
Applying Lemma \ref{lemma_abelian_section} to each fiber of $\rho_{/U_N}(M_R)$ over $\pi_{\mathrm{Siegel}}(M)$, we obtain that \begin{enumerate}
    \item[(a)] $\rho_{/U_N}(M_R)=\pi(M_0)\times \mathbb G_m^{t_0}$ where $t_0=\dim U_Q-\dim U_N$;
    \item[(b)] $\rho_{/U_N}(M_0)$ is a translation of $\pi(M_0)$ by $\sigma_N$, where $\sigma_N:\pi_{\mathrm{Siegel}}(M)\rightarrow \mathbb G_m^{t_0}$ is a morphism of varieties.
\end{enumerate}
By Proposition \ref{prop_normality_triviality}, $V^{\mathrm{ab}}_N$ is normal in $Q/U_N$. We may then further take the quotient of $M_{/U_N}$ by $V^{\mathrm{ab}}_N$. Then by a similar argument as in the proof of Theorem \ref{theorem_special_subvariety}, we obtain that $\sigma_N$ is a constant map to $0$. Therefore $\rho_{/U_N}(M_0)$ is an abelian $\pi_\mathrm{sab}(M)$-subscheme of $\rho_{/U_N}(M)$, its preimage $M_0$ is thus a semiabelian $\pi_{\mathrm{sab}}(M)$-subscheme of $M_R$, which concludes the proof.
<!-- end proof-8 -->
<!-- proposition-4: body_md -->
For any $y_\mathrm{sab}\in \pi_{\mathrm{sab}}(M)_{/p_{\mathrm{sab}}(N)}$, $$M'|_{\rho_{/p_{\mathrm{sab}}(N)}^{-1}(y_{\mathrm{sab}})}\rightarrow \rho_{/p_{\mathrm{sab}}(N)}^{-1}(y_{\mathrm{sab}})$$ is an isotrivial semiabelian scheme.
<!-- end proposition-4 -->
<!-- proof-9: body_md -->
Let $S$ be the image of $\rho_{/p_{\mathrm{sab}}(N)}^{-1}(y_{\mathrm{sab}})$ in $\mathbb A_g,$ $\mathcal A=\pi_{\mathrm{ab}}(M)|_S$, $\mathcal B=\rho^{-1}_{/p_{\mathrm{sab}}(N)}(y_\mathrm{sab})$, and $\mathcal G=\mathcal P_{g,t}^\times|_{\mathcal A\times_S\mathcal B}.$ Then $\mathcal G':=M_0|_{\mathcal B}$ is also a semiabelian subscheme of $\mathcal G$ over $\mathcal B$, i.e., we have the following commutative diagram
    \begin{equation*}
    \begin{tikzcd}
    0 \arrow[r] & T \arrow[d] \arrow[r] & \mathcal G' \arrow[d] \arrow[r] & \mathcal A'\times_S\mathcal B \arrow[d] \arrow[r] & 0 \\
    0 \arrow[r] & \mathbb G_m^t \arrow["\rho_{\mathrm{tor}}",d]  \arrow[r] & \mathcal{G} \arrow["\rho",d]  \arrow[r] & \mathcal A\times_S\mathcal B \arrow["\rho_{\mathrm{ab}}",d] \arrow[r] & 0,\\
    0 \arrow[r] & \mathbb G_m^t/T \arrow[r] & \mathcal{G}/\mathcal G'   \arrow[r] & (\mathcal A/\mathcal A')\times_S\mathcal B  \arrow[r] & 0,
    \end{tikzcd}
    \end{equation*}
    where $\mathcal A'=\pi_{\mathrm{ab}}(M_0)|_S.$
    Now it suffices to prove that $\mathcal G/\mathcal G'$ is isotrivial as $M'|_{\mathcal B}\subset \mathcal G/\mathcal G'$ as semiabelian subscheme.
    
    Let $\mathcal C$ be the isotrivial part of $\pi_{\mathrm{sab}}(M)|_S\rightarrow S$.
    Since $B$ is a weakly special subset, by \cite[Proposition 3.3]{ZG2017}, it is a translation of an abelian subscheme of $\pi_{\mathrm{sab}}(M)|_S$ by a torsion section and by a constant section of $\mathcal C\rightarrow S$. 

    By the theorem of the Fixed Part (see \cite[Theorem 1]{YA} or \cite[Corollaire 4.1.2]{PD}), $\mathcal A/\mathcal A'$ is isotrivial due to Proposition \ref{prop_normality_triviality}(2). After taking a finite cover of $S$, we may assume that $\mathcal A/\mathcal A'=A_0\times S$ for some abelian variety $A_0$ over $\mathbb{C}$. Then up to an isogeny, we may further assume that $\mathcal A=\mathcal A'\times A_0$. 
    
    For each $b\in \mathcal B$, we denote by $\gamma_b$ (resp. $\overline \gamma_b$) the extension class in $\mathrm{Ext}^1_{\mathbb{C}}(\mathcal A_b,\mathbb G_m^t)$ (resp. $\mathrm{Ext}_\mathbb{C}^1(A_0,\mathbb G_m^t/T)$) associated to $\mathcal G_b$ (resp. $(\mathcal G/\mathcal G')_b$), which satisfies the formula
    $$\rho_{\mathrm{tor},*}\gamma_b=\rho^*_{\mathrm{ab}}\overline \gamma_b \in \mathrm{Ext}^1(\mathcal A_b,\mathbb G_m^t/T).$$
    We first assume that $\mathcal B$ is an abelian subscheme of $\pi_{\mathrm{sab}}(M)|_S$. Again by Proposition \ref{prop_normality_triviality}(2) (more precisely, the formula \eqref{eq_poincare_pairing}), $$\gamma_b\in \mathrm{Im}(\mathrm{Ext}^1_\mathbb{C}(\mathcal A_b,T)\rightarrow \mathrm{Ext}^1_\mathbb{C}(\mathcal A_b,\mathbb G_m^t)),$$
    which forces that $\overline \gamma_b$ is torsion by applying the functor $\mathrm{Ext}^1(\mathcal A_b,\cdot)$ to $T\rightarrow \mathbb G_m^t\rightarrow \mathbb G_m^t/T$. 
    
    In the general case, $\overline\gamma_b$ is independent of $b$ up to torsion (determined by the constant section).
    We then conclude the proof by the Weil--Barsotti formula \cite[\S III.18]{Oort1966group}.
<!-- end proof-9 -->
<!-- definition-1: body_md -->
\label{def_algebraicity_uni_cover}
Let $\tilde{Y}$ be an analytic subvariety of $\mathcal X^+$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\widetilde{Y}$ is called an \emph{irreducible algebraic subset} of $\mathcal X^+$ if it is a complex analytically irreducible component of $Z\cap \mathcal X^+$ for some algebraic closed subset $Z\subset \mathcal X^\vee$;
\item $\widetilde{Y}$ is called \emph{algebraic} if it is a finite union of irreducible algebraic subsets of $\mathcal X^+$;
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end definition-1 -->
<!-- definition-2: body_md -->
\begin{enumerate}
        \item An irreducible subvariety $Z$ of $M$ is said to be \emph{bi-algebraic} if one (and hence any) complex analytic irreducible component of $\mathbf{u}^{-1}(Z)$ is algebraic in $\mathcal X^\vee$;
        \item For any subset $\Omega\subset M$, we denote by $\Omega^{\mathrm{biZar}}$ the smallest bi-algebraic subset containing $\Omega$. Define the \emph{weakly defect} of $\Omega$ as $$\delta_{\mathrm{ws}} (\Omega)=\dim(\Omega^\mathrm{biZar})-\dim(\Omega^\mathrm{Zar});$$
        \item Let $Y$ be a subvariety of $M$. We say an irreducible Zariski closed subvariety $Z\subset Y$ is \emph{weakly optimal} if for any irreducible Zariski closed subset $Z'\supsetneq Z$ of $Y$, $\delta_{\mathrm{ws}}(Z)<\delta_{\mathrm{ws}}(Z').$
    \end{enumerate}
<!-- end definition-2 -->
<!-- definition-3: body_md -->
\label{def_Weakly_Special}
A subvariety $Y$ of $M$ is called \emph{weakly special} if there exist\begin{enumerate}
    \item  a connected mixed Shimura subdatum $(Q,\mathcal Y^+)$ of $(P,\mathcal X^+)$,
    \item a connected normal subgroup $N$ of $Q$ whose reductive part is semisimple,
    \item and a point $\tilde{y}\in\mathcal Y^+$
\end{enumerate}
such that $Y=\mathbf{u}(N(\mathbb{R})^+U_N(\mathbb{C})\tilde{y})$, where $U_N=N\cap U$ and $U$ is the normal subgroup of $P$ of weight $-2$ part in \cite[Definition 2.1]{PinkThesis}. Equivalently, $Y$ is a fiber of the Shimura quotient map $\rho_{/N}.$

Note that weakly special subsets are precisely the bi-algebraic subsets due to \cite{UY2011Char} and \cite[Corollary 8.3]{ZGAxLindemann}
<!-- end definition-3 -->
<!-- remark-4: body_md -->
Let $(Q,\mathcal Y^+)$ be a connected mixed Shimura subdatum of $(P_{g,t},\mathcal X^+_{g,t}),$ and $N$ be a normal subgroup of $Q$. Then $U_N$ in Definition \ref{def_Weakly_Special} is exactly $N\cap \mathrm{M}_{t,1}.$
<!-- end remark-4 -->
<!-- theorem-7: body_md -->
\cite[Theorem 7.1]{BU}\label{Geometric_Zilber_Pink}
Let $Y\subset M$ be a subvariety. There exists a finite subset $$\Sigma_Y\subset\left\{(Q,\mathcal Y^+,N):\begin{aligned}
(Q,\mathcal Y^+)\text{ is a connected mixed Shimura}\\\text{ subdatum of }(P,\mathcal X^+),\text{ and } N \trianglelefteq Q\end{aligned}\right\}$$
such that for any weakly optimal subvariety $Z$ of $Y$, there exist $(Q,\mathcal Y^+,N)\in \Sigma_Y$ and $\widetilde y\in \mathcal Y^+$, such that 
$$Z^\mathrm{biZar}=\mathbf{u}(N(\mathbb{R})^+U_N(\mathbb{C})\widetilde y).$$
<!-- end theorem-7 -->
<!-- definitionproposition-1: body_md -->
Let $Y=\mathbf{u}(N(\mathbb{R})^+U_N(\mathbb{C})\widetilde y)\subset \mathcal P^\times_{g,t}$ be a weakly special subset.
    Then half of the \emph{the Betti rank} $$\frac{1}{2}\max_{\widetilde y\in \widetilde Y}\mathrm{rank}_\mathbb{R}(d\widetilde b|_{\widetilde Y})_{\widetilde y}$$ is independent of the choice of $\widetilde y$, which we denote as $h_N$.
<!-- end definitionproposition-1 -->
<!-- proof-10: body_md -->
For any $\widetilde y'\in \mathcal Y^+$, we have $q\cdot \widetilde y=\widetilde y'$ for some $q\in Q(\mathbb{R})^+U_Q(\mathbb{C})$. 
    Consider the map $\varphi:\mathcal X_{g,t}^+\rightarrow \mathcal X^+_{g,t}, x\mapsto q\cdot x.$
    Note that $$N(\mathbb{R})^+U_N(\mathbb{C})\widetilde y'=q N(\mathbb{R})^+U_N(\mathbb{C})q^{-1} q\cdot \widetilde y=qN(\mathbb{R})^+U_N(\mathbb{C})\widetilde y=\varphi(\widetilde Y)$$
    where the first equality is due to the normality of $N.$
    By the equivariance of the Betti map due to Proposition \ref{prop_betti_equivariant}, we obtain the diffeomorphism
    $\widetilde {\varphi}:\mathbb{C}^{t}\times \mathbb{R}^{2g}\rightarrow \mathbb{C}^{t}\times \mathbb{R}^{2g}$ such that $\widetilde b\circ \varphi=\widetilde\varphi\circ\widetilde b$, which concludes the proof.
<!-- end proof-10 -->
<!-- definition-4: body_md -->
Let $Y\subset \mathcal P_{g,t}^\times$ be a closed subvariety.
    We define the $r$\emph{-th degeneracy locus} $Y^{{\mathrm{deg}}}(r)$ as the union of all weakly optimal subvarieties $Z$ of $Y$ such that \begin{equation}\label{eq_defect_condition}\dim Z> h_N+r\end{equation}
    where $Z^\mathrm{biZar}=\mathbf{u}(N(\mathbb{R})^+U_N(\mathbb{C})\widetilde y)$ for some $(Q,\mathcal Y^+,N)\in \Sigma_Y$ and $\widetilde y\in \mathcal Y^+.$
<!-- end definition-4 -->
<!-- lemma-5: body_md -->
\label{lemma_biZar_weakly_optimal}
    Let $Z\subset Y$ be a weakly optimal subvariety. Then $Z$ is an irreducible component of $Z^{\mathrm{biZar}}\cap Y$.
<!-- end lemma-5 -->
<!-- proof-11: body_md -->
Let $Z'$ be an irreducible component $Z^\mathrm{biZar}\cap Y$ containing $Z$.
    Since $Z\subset Z'\subset Z^\mathrm{biZar}$, we obtain that $Z^\mathrm{biZar}\subset Z'^\mathrm{biZar}\subset Z^\mathrm{biZar}$, i.e., $Z^\mathrm{biZar}=Z'^\mathrm{biZar}$. 
    Hence $\delta_{\mathrm{ws}}(Z')=\dim (Z^{\mathrm{biZar}})-\dim Z'$. Assume that $Z\subsetneq Z'$, then $\delta_{\mathrm{ws}}(Z')>\delta_{\mathrm{ws}}(Z)$ by the weak optimality. Therefore $\dim Z'<\dim Z$, which is a contradiction. We thus obtain that $Z'=Z.$
<!-- end proof-11 -->
<!-- proposition-5: body_md -->
We have the equality
    \begin{equation}\label{eq_deg_loci_closed}
        \begin{aligned}
        Y^{{\mathrm{deg}}}(r)&=\bigcup_{(Q,\mathcal Y^+,N)\in \Sigma_Y} \{x\in Y\cap M:\dim_x  \rho^{-1}_{/N}\rho_{/N}(x)\cap (Y\cap M)> h_N+r \}
        \end{aligned}
    \end{equation}
    where $M$ is the Shimura subvariety given by $(Q,\mathcal Y^+)$ and $\rho_{/N}:M\rightarrow M_{/N}$ is the Shimura quotient map.
    In particular $Y^{{\mathrm{deg}}}(r)$ is Zariski-closed.
<!-- end proposition-5 -->
<!-- proof-12: body_md -->
Since $\dim_x  \rho^{-1}_{/N}\rho_{/N}(x)\cap (Y\cap M)$ is exactly the dimension of $\mathbf{u}(N(\mathbb{R})^+ U_N(\mathbb{C})\widetilde y)\cap Y$'s irreducible component $Y'$ which contains $x$, we have 
    $$\text{Right hand side of \eqref{eq_deg_loci_closed}}=\bigcup_{\substack{(Q,\mathcal Y^+,N)\in \Sigma_Y, \widetilde y\in \mathcal Y^+, Y'\subset \mathbf{u}(N(\mathbb{R})^+ U_N(\mathbb{C})\widetilde y)\cap Y,\\ Y'{\text{ irreducible and }} \dim Y'>h_N+r}} Y'$$
    
    We thus obtain the direction $"\subset"$ by Theorem \ref{Geometric_Zilber_Pink} and Lemma \ref{lemma_biZar_weakly_optimal}. 

    Conversely, let $Y'$ be an irreducible component of $\mathbf{u}(N(\mathbb{R})^+U_N(\mathbb{C})\widetilde y)\cap Y$ with $\dim Y'\geq h_N+r$. Then $Y'^{\mathrm{biZar}}\subset \mathbf{u}(N(\mathbb{R})^+U_N(\mathbb{C})\widetilde y)$. Therefore the generic Betti rank of $Y'^{\mathrm{biZar}}$ is not larger than $2h_N$, which implies that $Y'$ satisfies the condition \eqref{eq_defect_condition}. This concludes the proof.
<!-- end proof-12 -->
<!-- theorem-8: body_md -->
\label{theorem_non_deg_shimura_quotient}
    Let $Y\subset \mathcal P^\times_{g,t}$ be an irreducible closed subvariety. Then $Y^{{\mathrm{deg}}}(r)=Y$ if and only if there exists a triplet $(Q,\mathcal Y^+,N)\in \Sigma_Y$ such that
    $\dim Y-\dim \rho_{/N}(Y)> h_N+r.$
<!-- end theorem-8 -->
<!-- proof-13: body_md -->
This is a direct consequence of \eqref{eq_deg_loci_closed} and the irreducibility of $Y$.
<!-- end proof-13 -->
<!-- lemma-6: body_md -->
\label{lemm_weakly_optimal_maximality}
    Let $Z\subset Y$ be an irreducible closed subvariety. Assume that $\dim Z>h_N+r$ and $Z$ is maximal for this property. Then $Z$ is weakly optimal.
<!-- end lemma-6 -->
<!-- proof-14: body_md -->
Let $Z'$ be an irreducible closed subvariety of $Y$ such that $Z\subsetneq Z'$ and $\delta_{\mathrm{ws}}(Z)\geq \delta_{\mathrm{ws}}(Z')$. Since $$\dim Z^\mathrm{biZar}- h_N\leq \dim Z'^{\mathrm{biZar}}-h_{N'},$$ we obtained that $$\dim Z'^\mathrm{biZar}-\dim Z'\leq\dim Z^{\mathrm{biZar}}-\dim Z<\dim Z^{\mathrm{biZar}}-h_N-r\leq \dim Z'^{\mathrm{biZar}}-h_{N'}-r$$
    which implies that $\dim Z'>h_{N'}+r$, contradicting to the maximality of $Z$.
<!-- end proof-14 -->
<!-- proposition-6: body_md -->
\label{prop_bettirank_deg} Let $Y\subset \mathcal P_{g,t}^\times$ be an irreducible closed subvariety. If $r\geq 0$, then
    $Y^{\mathrm{deg}}(r)=Y$ if and only if $\displaystyle\max_{\widetilde y\in Y^{\mathrm{sm}}}\mathrm{rank}_{\mathbb{R}}(\widetilde b|_{\widetilde Y})_{\widetilde y}< 2 (\dim Y-r).$
<!-- end proposition-6 -->
<!-- proof-15: body_md -->
"$\Rightarrow$": Since $Y^{{\mathrm{deg}}}(r)=Y$, we see that there exists a triplet $(Q,\mathcal Y^+,N)\subset \Sigma_Y$ such that $\dim Y-\dim \rho_{/N}(Y)>h_N+r$ by Theorem \ref{theorem_non_deg_shimura_quotient}. For any $x\in Y^{\mathrm{sm}}$, let $Z$ be the irreducible component of $\rho_{/N}^{-1}\rho_{/N}(x)\cap Y$ containing $x$, hence $\dim Z>h_N+r$ for general $x$. 
    Then $$\begin{aligned}\mathrm{rank}_{\mathbb{R}}(d\widetilde b|_{\widetilde Y})_{\widetilde y}&\leq \mathrm{rank}_{\mathbb{R}}(d\widetilde b|_{\widetilde Z})_{\widetilde y}+2(\dim Y-\dim Z)\\&\leq \mathrm{rank}_\mathbb{R}(d\widetilde b|_{N(\mathbb{R})^+U_N(\mathbb{C})\widetilde y})_{\widetilde y}+2(\dim Y-\dim Z)\\&=2(h_N+\dim Y-\dim Z)<2(\dim Y-r).\end{aligned}$$

    "$\Leftarrow$": Assume that $\displaystyle\ell:=\max_{\widetilde y\in Y^{\mathrm{sm}}}\mathrm{rank}_{\mathbb{R}}(d\widetilde b|_{\widetilde Y})_{\widetilde y}< 2 (\dim Y-r)$. Then for any $x\in Y^{\mathrm{sm}}$, there exists a complex analytic set $\widetilde W\subset \widetilde b^{-1}(\widetilde b(\widetilde y))\cap \widetilde Y$ such that  $\dim \widetilde W\geq \dim Y-\ell>r$.
    Let $Z:=\mathbf{u}(\widetilde W)^\mathrm{Zar}$. By the Ax-Schaunuel theorem \cite[Theorem 1.1]{GaoKlingler2024AxSchanuel}, we have 
     $$\dim \widetilde W^{\mathrm{Zar}}+\dim Z\geq \dim \widetilde W+\dim Z^{\mathrm{biZar}}$$
    Since $\widetilde W^{\mathrm{Zar}}\subset \widetilde b^{-1}(\widetilde b(\widetilde{x}))\cap (N(\mathbb{R})^+U_N(\mathbb{C})\widetilde y)$, and the latter is algebraic and of dimension $\dim Z^\mathrm{biZar}-h_N$, we get $\dim Z\geq \dim W+h_N>r+h_N.$ By Lemma \ref{lemm_weakly_optimal_maximality}, $Z$ is contained in $Y^{{\mathrm{deg}}}(r)$, we are done.
<!-- end proof-15 -->
<!-- theorem-9: body_md -->
\label{theorem_quotient_subgrp_closure} Assume that $$\pi(M)=\pi_{\mathrm{ab}}(M)\times_{\pi_{\mathrm{Siegel}}(M)}\pi_{\mathrm{sab}}(M).$$Let $(Q,\mathcal Y^+)$ be the associated connected mixed Shimura datum of $M$. If $Y^{{\mathrm{deg}}}(r)=Y$, then there exists a normal subgroup $N\trianglelefteq Q$ with semisimple reductive part satisfying $N=(U_N\oplus V_N^\mathrm{ab})\cdot N$, such that 
$$\dim Y-\dim \rho_{/N}(Y)>h_N+r.$$
Moreover, \begin{equation}\label{eq_betti_rank}
h_{N}=\dim U_N+\frac{1}{2}\dim V^{\mathrm{ab}}_N,
\end{equation}
which is also the relative dimension of $M_0$ over $\pi_{\mathrm{sab}}(M)$ constructed in Corollary \ref{coro_semiabelian_subscheme}.
<!-- end theorem-9 -->
<!-- proof-16: body_md -->
By Theorem \ref{theorem_non_deg_shimura_quotient}, there exists $(Q^*,\mathcal Y^{+,*},N^*)\in \Sigma_Y$ such that $$\dim Y-\dim \rho_{/N^*}(Y)>h_{N^*}+r.$$
Let $M^*=\mathbf{u}(\mathcal Y^{+,*})$. Since $Y\subset M$, we have $M\subset M^*$. With out loss of generality, we may assume that $\mathcal Y^+\subset \mathcal Y^{+,*}$ and $Q<Q^*.$ Let $N$ be the neutral component of $Q\cap N^*.$ We may assume that the reductive part of $N$ is semisimple after replacing $N$ with $N\cap p_{\mathrm{Siegel}}^{-1}(p_{\mathrm{Siegel}}(N)^{\mathrm{der}})$, which is still normal in $Q$.

We have the following commutative diagram:
\[\begin{tikzcd}
    \widetilde Y &\mathcal Y^+ &\mathcal Y^{+,*}\\
	Y & M & M^*
                                         
	\arrow[from=1-1, to=1-2]
	\arrow[from=1-1, to=2-1]
	\arrow[hook,from=1-2, to=1-3]
	\arrow[from=1-2, to=2-2]
	\arrow[from=1-3, to=2-3]
	\arrow[from=2-1, to=2-2]
	\arrow[hook,from=2-2, to=2-3]
                             
                                      
                          
                          
                          
\end{tikzcd}\]
We denote by $\widetilde \rho_{/N}: \mathcal Y^+\rightarrow \mathcal Y^+/N$ (resp. $\widetilde \rho_{/N^*}: \mathcal Y^+\rightarrow \mathcal Y^{*,+}/N^*$) the map on the covering space induced by $\rho_{/N}$ (resp. $\rho_{/N^*}$).

Notice that the fiber of $\widetilde\rho_{/N}|_{\widetilde Y}$ are of form $$(U_N(\mathbb{C})N(\mathbb{R})^+\widetilde y)\cap \widetilde Y=((U_{N^*}(\mathbb{C})N^*(\mathbb{R})^+\widetilde y)\cap \mathcal Y^+)\cap \widetilde Y=((U_{N^*}(\mathbb{C})N^*(\mathbb{R})^+\widetilde y)\cap \widetilde Y,$$
while the fiber of $\widetilde \rho_{/N^*}|_{\widetilde Y}$ take the form of the right hand side. Therefore $\dim \rho_{/N^*}(Y)=\dim \rho_{/N}(Y)$. Since $N<N^*$, by definition, we have $h_N\leq h_{N^*}.$
Hence $$\dim Y-\dim \rho_{/N}(Y)=\dim Y-\dim \rho_{/N^*}(Y)>h_{N^*}+r\geq h_N+r,$$ we may thus replace $(Q^*,\mathcal Y^{+,*},N^*)$ with $(Q,\mathcal Y^+, N).$

On the other hand, we set $N':=(U_N\oplus V_N^\mathrm{ab})\cdot N$ which is normal by Proposition \ref{prop_normality_triviality}.(1). By the definition of $h_N$ and the equivariancy of Betti map due to Proposition \ref{prop_betti_equivariant}, we have \begin{equation*}
    h_{N'}=h_{N}=\dim U_N+\frac{1}{2}\dim V^{\mathrm{ab}}_N.
\end{equation*}
Hence we may further replace $N$ with $N'$, which concludes the proof
<!-- end proof-16 -->
<!-- definition-5: body_md -->
We denote by $\mathrm{Mod}.\dim_{\mathcal G}(S)$ the smallest dimension of quasi-projective variety $S'$ such that after taking a finite cover of $S$, there exists a morphism $f:S\rightarrow S'$ such that for each $s'\in S'$
    $$\mathcal G|_{f^{-1}(s')}\rightarrow f^{-1}(s')$$
    is an isotrivial family of semiabelian varieties.
<!-- end definition-5 -->
<!-- definition-6: body_md -->
Let $\mathcal X\subset \mathcal G$ be an irreducible closed subvariety.
    We say $\mathcal X$ is non-degenerate if for $Y:=\overline{\iota(\mathcal X)}$
    $$\max_{\widetilde y\in Y^{\mathrm{sm}}}\mathrm{rank}_{\mathbb{R}}(d\widetilde b|_{\widetilde Y})_{\widetilde y}=2\dim \mathcal X.$$
<!-- end definition-6 -->
<!-- theorem-10: body_md -->
\label{theo_nondeg_gen}
    Let $\overline\eta$ be the geometric generic point of $S$.
    Assume that 
        \begin{enumerate}
        \item $\iota^{[m]}|_{\mathcal X^{[m]}}$ is generically finite for $m\gg 0$.
        \item $\mathcal X_s$ generates $\mathcal A_s$ for each $s\in S;$
        \item $\mathcal X_{\overline \eta}$ is irreducible and has finite stabilizer.
    \end{enumerate}
    Then $\mathcal X^{[m]}$ is non-degenerate for every $m\gg 0.$
<!-- end theorem-10 -->
<!-- head-1: body_md -->
In order to prove Theorem \ref{theo_nondeg_gen}, it suffices to prove the following:
    \begin{theorem}\label{theorem_nondeg_group_quotient}
        We keep the same hypothesis as in Theorem \ref{theo_nondeg_gen}.
        For any $m\gg0$, let $\mathcal H\rightarrow \mathcal G^{[m]}$ be a semiabelian subscheme. Then either of the following holds:
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item[(i)] For general $s\in S$, $$\dim (\mathcal X^m_s/\mathcal H_s)\geq \dim (\mathcal X_s^m)-\dim \mathcal H_s+\dim S$$
        (see Notation and Conventions for the definition of $\mathcal X_s^m/\mathcal H_s$),
        \item[(ii)] or $\mathrm{Mod}.\dim _{\mathcal G^{[m]}/\mathcal H}(S)=\mathrm{Mod}.\dim_{\mathcal G}(S)$.
    \end{enumerate}
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 
    \end{theorem}
\begin{proof}[Proof of Theorem \ref{theorem_nondeg_group_quotient} $\Rightarrow$ Theorem \ref{theo_nondeg_gen}]
   Let $M\subset \mathcal P_{mg,mt}^\times$ be the smallest special subvariety containing $Y=\overline{\iota^{[m]}(\mathcal X^{[m]})}$.
    By hypothesis (2) in Theorem \ref{theo_nondeg_gen}, we obtain that 
    $\mathcal X^m_s$ generates $\mathcal A^m_s$ for any $s\in S$. Therefore
    $M$ satisfies the condition \eqref{eq_split_unipotent_radical} due to Lemma \ref{lemm_split_unipotnent_radical}. 
   Hence $M$ is a semiabelian subscheme of $\mathcal P_{mg,mt}^\times|_{\pi_{\mathrm{sab}}(M)}$ by Theorem \ref{theorem_special_subvariety}. Let $\mathcal G_{M}$ be the neutral component of $(\iota^{[m]})^{-1}(M\cap \iota^{[m]}(\mathcal G^{[m]})).$

    Let $(Q,\mathcal Y^+)$ be the Shimura subdatum of $M$. Assume that $\mathcal X^{[m]}$ is not non-degenerate, by Proposition \ref{prop_bettirank_deg}, $Y^{{\mathrm{deg}}}(0)=Y.$ Then there exists a normal subgroup $N$ of $Q$ with semisimple reductive part satisfying $N=(U_N\oplus V_N^\mathrm{ab})\cdot N$ such that \begin{equation}\label{eq_deg_contradiction}
        \dim Y-\dim\rho_{/N}(Y)>h_N
    \end{equation} due to Theorem \ref{theorem_quotient_subgrp_closure}.

    Let $M_0$ be the semiabelian subscheme of $M$ constructed in Corollary \ref{coro_semiabelian_subscheme}. 
    Put $\mathcal H$ to be the neutral component of $(\iota^{[m]})^{-1} (M_0\cap \iota^{[m]} (\mathcal G^{[m]}))\subset \mathcal G_M.$

In the case (i) of Theorem \ref{theorem_nondeg_group_quotient}, by the discussion on two steps quotient of $\rho_{/N}$ in \eqref{eq_two_steps_quotient}, \begin{align*}
    \dim \rho_{/N}(Y)&\geq \dim (Y/M_0)_{\iota_S(s)}= \dim (Y/\iota^{[m]}(\mathcal H))_{\iota_S(s)}\\
    &\geq\dim (\mathcal X_s^m/\mathcal H_s)\\
    &\geq \dim (\mathcal X_s^m)-\dim \mathcal H_s +\dim S\\
    &\geq\dim Y_{\iota_S(s)}-\dim (M_0)_{\iota_S(s)}+\dim \iota_S(S)\\
    &=\dim Y-h_N
\end{align*}
for general $s\in S$, where the first and second equality is due to hypothesis (1) in Theorem \ref{theo_nondeg_gen}, and the last equality is due to \eqref{eq_betti_rank}. This is a contradiction to \eqref{eq_deg_contradiction}.

As for the case (ii), 
since $\pi_{\mathcal G^{[m]}/\mathcal A^{[m]}}(\mathcal G_M)=\mathcal A^{[m]}$ by condition (2) of Theorem \ref{theo_nondeg_gen}, $\mathcal G$ is isogeneous to $\mathcal G_M\times \mathbb G_m^{t'}$ for some $0\leq t'\leq t.$ Hence $\mathcal G/\mathcal H$ is isogeneous to $(\mathcal G_M/\mathcal H)\times \mathbb G_m^{t'}$. Therefore $$\mathrm{Mod}.\dim_{\mathcal G_M/\mathcal H}(S)=\mathrm{Mod}.\dim_{\mathcal G/\mathcal H}(S)\overset{\text{by (ii)}}{=}\mathrm{Mod}.\dim_{\mathcal G}(S)=\dim \iota_S(S).$$ Thus by the discussion before \eqref{eq_two_steps_quotient}, we obtain that $$\dim \rho_{/_{p_{\mathrm{sab}}(N)}}(\iota_S(S))=\dim \iota_S(S)$$ due to the minimality of $\mathrm{Mod}.\dim _{\mathcal G/\mathcal H}(S).$ Moreover, \eqref{eq_two_steps_quotient} again gives that
$$\dim \rho_{/N}(Y)=\dim (Y/M_0)|_{\iota_S(S)}=\dim Y-h_N$$
which also contradicts \eqref{eq_deg_contradiction}.
\end{proof}

From now on to the end of this section, let $\mathcal H$ be a semiabelian subscheme of $\mathcal G^{[m]}$ given by the following commutative diagram:
    \begin{equation}\label{eq_semiabelian_subscheme}
    \begin{tikzcd}
    0 \arrow[r] & T \arrow[d] \arrow[r] & \mathcal{H} \arrow[d] \arrow[r] & \mathcal A_{\mathcal H} \arrow[d] \arrow[r] & 0 \\
    0 \arrow[r] & (\mathbb G_m^t)^m \arrow[r] & \mathcal{G}^{[m]} \arrow[r] & \mathcal A^{[m]} \arrow[r] & 0
    \end{tikzcd},
    \end{equation}
<!-- end head-1 -->
<!-- theorem-11: body_md -->
\label{theorem_nondeg_group_quotient}
        We keep the same hypothesis as in Theorem \ref{theo_nondeg_gen}.
        For any $m\gg0$, let $\mathcal H\rightarrow \mathcal G^{[m]}$ be a semiabelian subscheme. Then either of the following holds:
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item[(i)] For general $s\in S$, $$\dim (\mathcal X^m_s/\mathcal H_s)\geq \dim (\mathcal X_s^m)-\dim \mathcal H_s+\dim S$$
        (see Notation and Conventions for the definition of $\mathcal X_s^m/\mathcal H_s$),
        \item[(ii)] or $\mathrm{Mod}.\dim _{\mathcal G^{[m]}/\mathcal H}(S)=\mathrm{Mod}.\dim_{\mathcal G}(S)$.
    \end{enumerate}
<!-- end theorem-11 -->
<!-- proof-17: body_md -->
Let $M\subset \mathcal P_{mg,mt}^\times$ be the smallest special subvariety containing $Y=\overline{\iota^{[m]}(\mathcal X^{[m]})}$.
    By hypothesis (2) in Theorem \ref{theo_nondeg_gen}, we obtain that 
    $\mathcal X^m_s$ generates $\mathcal A^m_s$ for any $s\in S$. Therefore
    $M$ satisfies the condition \eqref{eq_split_unipotent_radical} due to Lemma \ref{lemm_split_unipotnent_radical}. 
   Hence $M$ is a semiabelian subscheme of $\mathcal P_{mg,mt}^\times|_{\pi_{\mathrm{sab}}(M)}$ by Theorem \ref{theorem_special_subvariety}. Let $\mathcal G_{M}$ be the neutral component of $(\iota^{[m]})^{-1}(M\cap \iota^{[m]}(\mathcal G^{[m]})).$

    Let $(Q,\mathcal Y^+)$ be the Shimura subdatum of $M$. Assume that $\mathcal X^{[m]}$ is not non-degenerate, by Proposition \ref{prop_bettirank_deg}, $Y^{{\mathrm{deg}}}(0)=Y.$ Then there exists a normal subgroup $N$ of $Q$ with semisimple reductive part satisfying $N=(U_N\oplus V_N^\mathrm{ab})\cdot N$ such that \begin{equation}\label{eq_deg_contradiction}
        \dim Y-\dim\rho_{/N}(Y)>h_N
    \end{equation} due to Theorem \ref{theorem_quotient_subgrp_closure}.

    Let $M_0$ be the semiabelian subscheme of $M$ constructed in Corollary \ref{coro_semiabelian_subscheme}. 
    Put $\mathcal H$ to be the neutral component of $(\iota^{[m]})^{-1} (M_0\cap \iota^{[m]} (\mathcal G^{[m]}))\subset \mathcal G_M.$

In the case (i) of Theorem \ref{theorem_nondeg_group_quotient}, by the discussion on two steps quotient of $\rho_{/N}$ in \eqref{eq_two_steps_quotient}, \begin{align*}
    \dim \rho_{/N}(Y)&\geq \dim (Y/M_0)_{\iota_S(s)}= \dim (Y/\iota^{[m]}(\mathcal H))_{\iota_S(s)}\\
    &\geq\dim (\mathcal X_s^m/\mathcal H_s)\\
    &\geq \dim (\mathcal X_s^m)-\dim \mathcal H_s +\dim S\\
    &\geq\dim Y_{\iota_S(s)}-\dim (M_0)_{\iota_S(s)}+\dim \iota_S(S)\\
    &=\dim Y-h_N
\end{align*}
for general $s\in S$, where the first and second equality is due to hypothesis (1) in Theorem \ref{theo_nondeg_gen}, and the last equality is due to \eqref{eq_betti_rank}. This is a contradiction to \eqref{eq_deg_contradiction}.

As for the case (ii), 
since $\pi_{\mathcal G^{[m]}/\mathcal A^{[m]}}(\mathcal G_M)=\mathcal A^{[m]}$ by condition (2) of Theorem \ref{theo_nondeg_gen}, $\mathcal G$ is isogeneous to $\mathcal G_M\times \mathbb G_m^{t'}$ for some $0\leq t'\leq t.$ Hence $\mathcal G/\mathcal H$ is isogeneous to $(\mathcal G_M/\mathcal H)\times \mathbb G_m^{t'}$. Therefore $$\mathrm{Mod}.\dim_{\mathcal G_M/\mathcal H}(S)=\mathrm{Mod}.\dim_{\mathcal G/\mathcal H}(S)\overset{\text{by (ii)}}{=}\mathrm{Mod}.\dim_{\mathcal G}(S)=\dim \iota_S(S).$$ Thus by the discussion before \eqref{eq_two_steps_quotient}, we obtain that $$\dim \rho_{/_{p_{\mathrm{sab}}(N)}}(\iota_S(S))=\dim \iota_S(S)$$ due to the minimality of $\mathrm{Mod}.\dim _{\mathcal G/\mathcal H}(S).$ Moreover, \eqref{eq_two_steps_quotient} again gives that
$$\dim \rho_{/N}(Y)=\dim (Y/M_0)|_{\iota_S(S)}=\dim Y-h_N$$
which also contradicts \eqref{eq_deg_contradiction}.
<!-- end proof-17 -->
<!-- proposition-7: body_md -->
\label{prop_isogeny_induction}
     Let $\mathcal B\subset \mathcal T$ be a semiabelian subscheme. Assume that there exists an isogeny $h_{\mathcal T}:\mathcal T\rightarrow \mathcal T$ satisfying the following:
    \begin{itemize}
        \item[(a)] $h_{\mathcal T}(\mathcal B)=\mathcal B_1\times_S \mathcal B_1'^\perp$, where $\mathcal B_1:=p_{1,\mathcal T}(h_{\mathcal T}(\mathcal B))$ and $\mathcal B_1'^\perp=p_{1,\mathcal T}^\perp(h_{\mathcal T}(\mathcal B))$;
        \item[(b)] There exists another isogeny $h_{1,\mathcal T}:\mathcal T_1\rightarrow \mathcal T_1$ such that $h_{1,\mathcal T}p_{1,\mathcal T}=p_{1,\mathcal T}h_{\mathcal T}$, i.e., the following diagram:
        \[
\begin{tikzcd}
  \mathcal T \ar[d,"p_{1,\mathcal T}"'] \ar[r,"h_{\mathcal T}"] & \mathcal T \ar[d,"p_{1,\mathcal T}"] \\
  \mathcal T_1 \ar[r,"h_{1,\mathcal T}"'] &  \mathcal T_1
\end{tikzcd}
\]
    \end{itemize}
    Let $\mathcal B_1^\perp$ be the neutral component of $h_{\mathcal T}^{-1}(\epsilon_S\times_S \mathcal B_1'^\perp)$. Put $\mathcal X:=\mathcal X_1\times_{\mathcal X_0}\mathcal X_1^\perp \subset \mathcal G$.
    Then
    $$\dim ((\mathcal X/\mathcal B)_w)\geq \dim (\mathcal X_1)_w-\dim (\mathcal B_1)_s+ \dim ((\mathcal X_1^\perp/\mathcal B_1^\perp)_w)+\begin{cases}
    1  \qquad \text{if }\mathcal B_1\not=0,\\
    0   \qquad \text{otherwise}
\end{cases}$$
for general $w\in \mathcal X_0$ and $s=\pi_{\mathcal G_0/S}(w).$
<!-- end proposition-7 -->
<!-- proof-18: body_md -->
We do the fiberwise pushout over $S$ for the isogeny $h_{\mathcal T}:\mathcal T\to\mathcal T$, to a $\mathcal G_0$-invariant isogeny
$h:\mathcal G\to\mathcal G'.$
Let $\mathcal G_1'$ (resp. $\mathcal G_1'^\perp$) be the pushout of $\mathcal G'$ along $p_{1,\mathcal T}$ (resp. $p_{1,\mathcal T}^\perp$), and denote by $p_1':\mathcal G'\to \mathcal G_1'$ (resp. $p_1'^\perp:\mathcal G'\to \mathcal G_1'^\perp$) the induced projection. By condition (b), there is an isogeny $h_1:\mathcal G_1\to \mathcal G_1'$
such that
\begin{equation}\label{eq_isogeny_cd}
h_1\circ p_1 = p_1'\circ h.    
\end{equation}

Consider the quotient
\[
\mathcal G'/h(\mathcal B)=(\mathcal G_1'/\mathcal B_1)\times_{\mathcal G_0}(\mathcal G_1'^\perp/\mathcal B_1'^\perp),\]
and the induced isogeny $\overline h:\mathcal G/\mathcal B\rightarrow \mathcal G'/h(\mathcal B)$. Let
$\overline p_1':\mathcal G'/h(\mathcal B)\to \mathcal G_1'/\mathcal B_1$
be the first projection. Then we have the following commuative diagram
\[
\begin{tikzpicture}[
  scale=1.1,
  every node/.style={font=\small},
  >=stealth
]
                 
\node (GB) at (0,0) {$\mathcal G/\mathcal B$};
\node (G1B) at (3.5,0) {$\mathcal G_1/p_1(\mathcal B)$};
\node (GpB) at (1.4,1.6) {$\mathcal G'/h(\mathcal B)$};
\node (G1pB) at (4.9,1.6) {$\mathcal G_1'/\mathcal B_1$};

                    
\node (G) at (0,2.5) {$\mathcal G$};
\node (G1) at (3.5,2.5) {$\mathcal G_1$};
\node (Gp) at (1.4,4.1) {$\mathcal G'$};
\node (G1p) at (4.9,4.1) {$\mathcal G_1'$};

              
\draw[->] (G) -- node[below] {$p_1$} (G1);
\draw[->] (G) -- node[left] {$h$} (Gp);
\draw[->] (G1) -- node[right] {$h_1$} (G1p);
\draw[->] (Gp) -- node[above] {$p_1'$} (G1p);

           
\draw[->] (GB) -- node[below] {$\overline p_1$} (G1B);
\draw[->] (GB) -- node[left] {$\overline h$} (GpB);
\draw[->] (G1B) -- node[right] {$\overline h_1$} (G1pB);
\draw[->] (GpB) -- node[above] {$\overline p_1'$} (G1pB);

                                                
\draw[->] (G) -- node[left] {} (GB);
\draw[->] (G1) -- node[right] {} (G1B);
\draw[->] (Gp) -- node[left] {} (GpB);
\draw[->] (G1p) -- node[right] {} (G1pB);

\end{tikzpicture}
\]
Then by \eqref{eq_isogeny_cd},
\[
\overline p'_1\bigl(\overline h(\mathcal X/\mathcal B)\bigr)=\overline p'_1\bigl(h(\mathcal X)/h(\mathcal B)\bigr)=h_1(\mathcal X_1)/\mathcal B_1.
\]
Hence for a general point $z\in h_1(\mathcal X_1)_w$ with $\overline z$ being its image in $h_1(\mathcal X_1)_s/(\mathcal B_1)_s$, we have
\[
\begin{aligned}\allowdisplaybreaks
\dim\bigl(\overline h(\mathcal X/\mathcal B)_w\bigr)&\ge\dim\bigl((h_1(\mathcal X_1)/\mathcal B_1)_w\bigr)+\dim\Bigl({\overline p'_1}^{-1}(\overline z)\cap \overline h(\mathcal X/\mathcal B)_w\Bigr)\\
&\ge\dim(\mathcal X_1)_w - \dim(\mathcal B_1)_s+\dim\Bigl({\overline p'_1}^{-1}(\overline z)\cap \overline h(\mathcal X/\mathcal B)_w\Bigr)\\
&\kern 7em+\begin{cases}
    1  \qquad \text{if }\mathcal B_1\not=0,\\
    0   \qquad \text{otherwise}
\end{cases},
\end{aligned}
\]
where the last inequality follows from condition (iii) for $\mathcal X_1$.

Now notice that
\[
{\overline p'_1}^{-1}(\overline z)\cap \overline h(\mathcal X/\mathcal B)_w=\overline h((\mathcal X/\mathcal B)\cap \overline h^{-1}{\overline p'_1}^{-1}(\overline z))=\overline h((\mathcal X/\mathcal B)\cap \overline p_1^{-1}\overline h_1^{-1}(\overline z))
\]
where the second equality is due to \eqref{eq_isogeny_cd}.
Therefore 
$$
\begin{aligned}\allowdisplaybreaks
    {\overline p'_1}^{-1}(\overline z)\cap \overline h(\mathcal X/\mathcal B)_w&=\overline h((p_1^{-1}h_1^{-1}(z)\cap \mathcal X)/\mathcal B_s)\\
    &\kern-2em=\bigcup_{y\in \mathcal X_1\cap h_1^{-1}(z)} \overline h\big(\left(\{y\}\times(\mathcal X_1^\perp)_w\right)/\mathcal B_s\big)
\end{aligned}
$$
where the first equality holds since $$(p_1^{-1}h_1^{-1}(z+(\mathcal B_1)_s)\cap \mathcal X)/\mathcal B_s=(p_1^{-1}h_1^{-1}(z)\cap\mathcal X)/\mathcal B_s.$$
As $\mathcal X_1\cap h_1^{-1}(z)$ is a finite set, we only need to estimate $\dim ((\{y\}\times(\mathcal X_1^\perp)_w)/\mathcal B_s)$.

We take arbitrary $y'\in \{y\}\times (\mathcal G_1^\perp)_w$,
Then 
\begin{align*}\allowdisplaybreaks\dim ((\{y\}\times(\mathcal X_1^\perp)_w)/\mathcal B_s)&=\dim ((\{y\}\times(\mathcal X_1^\perp)_w-y')/\mathcal B_s)
\end{align*}
Observe that \begin{align*}
    \{y\}\times(\mathcal X_1^\perp)_w-y'=\{e_1\}\times ((\mathcal X_1^\perp)_s-p_1^{\perp}(y'))_{e_0}
\end{align*}
where $e_1$ (resp. $e_0$) stands for the identity in $(\mathcal G_1)_s$ (resp. $(\mathcal G_0)_s$). Therefore \begin{align*}
\dim ((\{y\}\times(\mathcal X_1^\perp)_w)/\mathcal B_s)&=\dim (((\mathcal X_1^\perp)_s-p_1^{\perp}(y'))_{e_0}/(\{e_1'\}\times (\mathcal T_1^\perp)_s\cap\mathcal B_s))\\
&=\dim ((\mathcal X_1^\perp/\mathcal B_1^\perp)_{w})
\end{align*}
where $e_1'$ stands for the identity in $(\mathcal T_1)_s$. The last equality is due to the facts that 
\begin{align*}
    \mathcal B_1^\perp&=\text{neutral component of }h_{\mathcal T}^{-1}(\epsilon_S\times_S \mathcal B_1'^\perp)\\&=\text{neutral component of }\mathcal B\cap h_{\mathcal T}^{-1}(\epsilon_S\times_S\mathcal T_1^\perp).
\end{align*}
and $(e_S\times_S T_1^\perp)\cap \mathcal B\subset \mathcal B\cap h_{\mathcal T}^{-1}(\epsilon_S\times_S\mathcal T_1^\perp)$ by hypothesis (b), which thus contains $\mathcal B_1^\perp$ as a subgroup of finite index by dimension reason.
<!-- end proof-18 -->
<!-- proposition-8: body_md -->
\label{prop_torus_quotient}
    Let $h_{\mathrm{tor}}$ be an isogeny as in Proposition \ref{prop_isogeny_trick} applying to $T\subset (\mathbb G_m^t)^m$ such that after reordering factors of $(\mathbb G_m^t)^m$, $h_{\mathrm{tor}}(T)=T_1\times \cdots\times T_m$ and $T_i\not=0$ if and only if $i\leq m_{\mathrm{tor}}$ for some $m_{\mathrm{tor}}$.
    Then $$\dim (\mathcal X_s^m/\mathcal H_s)\geq \dim \mathcal X_s^m-\dim \mathcal H_s+m_{\mathrm{tor}}$$
    for general $s\in S.$
<!-- end proposition-8 -->
<!-- proof-19: body_md -->
Notice that 
$$\dim (\mathcal X_s^m/\mathcal H_s)\geq\dim (\mathcal X^m_s/T)-\dim (\mathcal A_{\mathcal H})_s$$
and $\dim (\mathcal X^m_s/T)\geq \dim (\mathcal X^m_w/T)+\dim \pi(X)^m_s$ for general $w\in \pi(\mathcal X)^m_s$.
It suffices to prove that \begin{equation}\label{eq_torus_quotient_fiber_dim}
    \dim (\mathcal X^m_w/T)\geq\dim (\mathcal X_w^m)-\dim T+m_{\mathrm{tor}}
\end{equation}
for general $s\in S$ and $w\in \pi(\mathcal X)^m.$

We proceed by induction on $m$. In the case that $m=1$ is due to the condition (3) in Theorem \ref{theo_nondeg_gen}.
Now assume that $m\geq 2$. We may further assume that $m_{\mathrm{tor}}>0$ since there is nothing to prove if $m_\mathrm{tor}=0.$
We briefly explain that we are in the situation as \S \ref{subsection_induction_step} by the substitution
\[\begin{cases}\allowdisplaybreaks
    \mathcal T_1=\mathbb G_{m,S}^t, \\\mathcal G_1=\mathcal G\times_S \mathcal A^{[m-1]},\\
    \mathcal T_1^\perp=(\mathbb G_m^t)^{m-1}\times S,\\
    \mathcal G_1^\perp=\mathcal A\times_S\mathcal G^{[m-1]},\\
    \mathcal X_1=\mathcal X\times_S \pi(\mathcal X)^{[m-1]},\\ \mathcal X_1^\perp=\pi(\mathcal X)\times_S \mathcal X^{[m-1]}.
\end{cases}
\]
Note that here $\mathcal G_0=\mathcal A^{[m]}$. Applying Proposition \ref{prop_isogeny_induction} for $\mathcal B=T\times S$, we obtain that 
for general $w\in \pi(\mathcal X)^{[m]},$
\begin{equation}\label{eq_torus_quotient_fiber_dim_1}\dim (\mathcal X_w^m/T)\geq \dim (\mathcal X_1)_w-\dim (T_1)+\dim ((\mathcal X_1^\perp)_w/ T_1^\perp)+1.\end{equation}
Here $T_1^\perp$ is the neutral component of $h_{\mathrm{tor}}^{-1}(\{0\}\times T_2\times\cdots T_m)$.

Since $(\mathcal X_1)_w\simeq \mathcal X_{p_1(w)}$ and $(\mathcal X_1^\perp)_w\simeq\mathcal X^{[m-1]}_{(p_2,\dots,p_m)(w)}$, applying the induction hypothesis to $h_{\mathrm{tor}}^{(1)}$ (see the notation in Proposition \ref{prop_isogeny_trick}(3)) and $T_1^\perp$, we obtain that 
$$\dim ((\mathcal X_1^\perp)_w/ T_1^\perp)\geq \dim (\mathcal X^{[m-1]}_{(p_2,\dots,p_m)(w)})-\sum_{2\leq i\leq m}\dim T_i+m_\mathrm{tor}-1.$$
Combining with \eqref{eq_torus_quotient_fiber_dim_1}, we obtain \eqref{eq_torus_quotient_fiber_dim}, which concludes the proof.
<!-- end proof-19 -->
<!-- proposition-9: body_md -->
\label{prop_abel_quotient} Assume that $\mathcal B\subset \mathcal G^{[m]}$ is an abelian subscheme. Then either
 $$\dim(\mathcal X_s^m/\mathcal B_s)\geq \dim \mathcal X^{[m]}-\dim \mathcal B+m$$
for general $s\in S$, or $\mathrm{Mod}.\dim_{\mathcal G^{[m]}/\mathcal B}(S)=\mathrm{Mod}.\dim_{\mathcal G}(S).$
<!-- end proposition-9 -->
<!-- proof-20: body_md -->
Applying Proposition \ref{prop_isogeny_trick} to the generic fiber $\mathcal B_\eta\subset \mathcal G_\eta^m$, we obtain an isogeny $h:\mathcal G^m_\eta\rightarrow \mathcal G_\eta^m$  We may assume that $S$ is normal after replacing $S$ with its normalization.
Then by \cite[Chapter I, Proposition 2.7]{FalitngsChai}, $h$ induces an isogeny $\mathcal G^{[m]}\rightarrow \mathcal G^{[m]}$, which we still denote as $h$, such that the properties in Proposition \ref{prop_isogeny_trick} are preserved. We recall here:
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item $h(\mathcal B)=\mathcal B_1\times \cdots\times \mathcal B_m$ where $\mathcal B_i=p_{i}(h(\mathcal B));$
        \item $\mathcal B_i\not=0$ if and only if $i\leq m'$ for some $0\leq m'\leq m;$
        \item For each $i=0,\dots, m-1$, $h$ preserves the subgroup $\mathrm{ker}(p_{1},\dots,p_i)$. We denote the induced isogeny on $\mathrm{ker}(p_{1},\dots,p_i)\simeq \mathcal G^{[m-i]}$ as $h^{(i)}.$ Moreover $h^{(m')}$ is the multiplication by $n$ map for some $n>0;$ 
        \item For each $i=1,\dots,m$ there exists an isogeny $h_i:\mathcal G\rightarrow \mathcal G$ such that 
        $$h_i\circ p_{i}= p_{i}\circ h^{(i-1)}.$$
    \end{enumerate}
We first consider the case that $m'<m$.
After identifying $\mathrm{ker}(p_1,\dots,p_{m'})$ with $\mathcal G^{[m-m']}$, by condition (3), we have $\mathcal G^{[m]}/h(\mathcal B)=\mathcal G^{[m-m']}\times_S \mathcal G'$ for some semiabelian scheme $\mathcal G'$ over $S$.
Therefore $$\mathrm{Mod}.\dim_{\mathcal G^{[m]}/\mathcal B}(S)=\mathrm{Mod}.\dim_{\mathcal G^{[m]}/h(\mathcal B)}(S)=\mathrm{Mod}.\dim_{\mathcal G}(S).$$

From now on, we assume that $m=m'$. We proceed by induction on $m$. The case that $m=1$ is trivial . Now we assume that $m\geq 2$. Similarly as in previous subsection, we consider the following substitution according to the notations in \S \ref{subsection_induction_step}:
\[\begin{cases}
    \mathcal G_0=S,\\
    \mathcal T_1=\mathcal G_1=\mathcal G,\\
    \mathcal T_1^\perp=\mathcal G_1^\perp=\mathcal G^{[m-1]},\\
    \mathcal X_1=\mathcal X,\\
    \mathcal X_1^\perp=\mathcal X^{[m-1]}.
\end{cases}\]
Then Proposition \ref{prop_isogeny_induction} gives that 
\begin{equation}\label{eq_quotient_abel_fiber_dim}
    \dim (\mathcal X_s^m/\mathcal B_s)\geq \dim \mathcal X_s-\dim (\mathcal B_1)_s+\dim (\mathcal X^{m-1}_s/(\mathcal B_1^\perp)_s)+1
\end{equation}
where $\mathcal B_1^\perp$ is the neutral component of $h^{-1}(\epsilon_S\times_S \mathcal B_2\times_S\cdots\times_S\mathcal B_m).$ By induction hypothesis, $$\dim (\mathcal X_s^{m-1}/(\mathcal B_1^\perp)_s)\geq \dim (\mathcal X^{[m-1]})-\dim (\mathcal B_1^\perp)+m-1$$
which concludes the proof by combining with \eqref{eq_quotient_abel_fiber_dim}.
<!-- end proof-20 -->
<!-- proof-21: body_md -->
Applying the Proposition \ref{prop_isogeny_trick} to $T$ and $(\mathbb G_m^t)^m$, we obtain an isogeny $h_{\mathrm{tor}}:(\mathbb G_m^t)^m\rightarrow (\mathbb G_m^t)^m$ such that \begin{enumerate}
        \item $h_{\mathrm{tor}}(T)=T_1\times \cdots \times T_m$ where $T_i$ is the projection of $h_{\mathrm{tor}}(T)$ on the $i$-th $\mathbb G_m^t.$
        \item For each $i$ such that $T_i=0$, the restriction of $h_\mathrm{tor}$ on the $i$-th $\mathbb G_m^t$ is the multiplication by $n$ map.
    \end{enumerate}
    Let $\mathcal G'$ be the pushout of $\mathcal G^{[m]}$ along $h_{\mathrm{tor}}$, which yields an isogeny $h:\mathcal G^{[m]}\rightarrow \mathcal G'.$ 
    
    Without loss of generality, we may assume that $T_i\not=0$ if and only if $i\leq m_\mathrm{tor}$ for some $0\leq m_{\mathrm{tor}}\leq m.$ We abbreviate by $\mathcal G^{[m-m_\mathrm{tor}]}$ the fiber product of the last $m-m_{\mathrm{tor}}$ $\mathcal G$'s over $S$, and by $p:\mathcal G^{[m]}\rightarrow \mathcal G^{[m_\mathrm{tor}]}$ the quotient map.
    By the construction and condition (2) above, the restriction of $h$ on $\mathcal G^{[m-m_\mathrm{tor}]}$ is the multiplication by $n$ map.
    
    Let $\mathcal B$ be the neutral component of $h(\mathcal H)\cap \mathcal G^{[m-m_\mathrm{tor}]}$, which is a semiabelian subscheme of $\mathcal G^{[m-m_\mathrm{tor}]}$. The torus part of $\mathcal B$ is contained in $(\mathbb G_m^t)^{m-m_\mathrm{tor}}\cap h_{\mathrm{tor}}(T)=0$, i.e., $\mathcal B$ is an abelian subscheme.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              
We have the following diagram \begin{equation}\label{eq_cd_quotient_isogeny}
\begin{tikzcd}
0 \ar[r] & \mathcal G^{[m-m_{\mathrm{tor}}]} \ar[r] \ar[d, "\lbrack n\rbrack"] & \mathcal G^{[m]} \ar[r,"p"] \ar[d, "h"] & \mathcal G^{[m_{\mathrm{tor}}]} \ar[r] \ar[d,"h'"] & 0 \\
0 \ar[r] &
\mathcal G^{[m-m_{\mathrm{tor}}]} \ar[r] \ar[d] &
\mathcal G' \ar[r, "p'"] \ar[d] &
\mathcal G'' \ar[r] \ar[d] &
0 \\
0 \ar[r] & \mathcal G^{[m-m_{\mathrm{tor}}]}/\mathcal B \ar[r] & \mathcal G'/h(\mathcal H) \ar[r,"\overline p'"] & \mathcal G''/h'(p(\mathcal H)) \ar[r] & 0
\end{tikzcd}
\end{equation}
where $\mathcal G''=\mathcal G'/\mathcal G^{[m-m_\mathrm{tor}]},$ and $h':\mathcal G^{[m_\mathrm{tor}}]\rightarrow \mathcal G''$ is an $\mathcal A^{[m_\mathrm{tor}]}$-invariant isogeny. Remark that the bottom left square is not necessarily a pull-back, but since $\mathcal B$ is of finite index in $\mathrm{ker}(p')$, this does affect our dimension arguments.

    Therefore \begin{equation}\label{eq_torus_fiber_dim}
        \begin{aligned}
        \dim (\mathcal X_s^{m}/\mathcal H_s)&=\dim (h(\mathcal X^{m}_s)/h(\mathcal H_s))\\
        &\geq\dim \overline p'(h(\mathcal X_s^m)/h(\mathcal H_s))+\dim (\overline p'^{-1}(\overline {h'(y)})\cap (h(\mathcal X_s^m)/h(\mathcal H_s)))
    \end{aligned}
    \end{equation}
    for general $s\in S$, $y\in p(\mathcal X_s^m)=\mathcal X_s^{m_\mathrm{tor}}$, and $\overline {h'(y)}$ being its image in $\mathcal G''/h'(p(\mathcal H)).$

    We first see that 
    \begin{equation}\label{eq_abelian_quot_dim}
        \begin{aligned}\dim \overline p'(h(\mathcal X_s^m)/h(\mathcal H_s))&=\dim (h'(p(\mathcal X_s^m))/h'(p(\mathcal H_s)))\\&=\dim (h'(\mathcal X_s^{m_{\mathrm{tor}}})/h'(p(\mathcal H_s)))\\&\geq \dim (\mathcal X_s^{m_{\mathrm{tor}}})-\dim p(\mathcal H_s)+m_{\mathrm{tor}}
    \end{aligned}
    \end{equation}
    where the inequality is due to Proposition \ref{prop_torus_quotient}.
    
    On the other hand, for general $s\in S$ and $y\in \mathcal X^{[m_\mathrm{tor}]},$
    \begin{align*}
        &\dim (\overline p'^{-1}(\overline {h'(y)})\cap \big(h(\mathcal X_s^m)/h(\mathcal H_s)\big))=\dim (\big(p^{-1}(y)\cap \mathcal X_s^m\big)/\mathcal H_s)\\
        &\kern 3em=\dim \big(\mathcal X_s^{m-m_{\mathrm{tor}}}+(z_1,\dots,z_{m-m_\mathrm{tor}})\big)/(\mathcal H_s\cap \mathcal G_s^{m-m_\mathrm{tor}})\\
        &\kern 3em=\dim \left(\big((\mathcal X_s-z_1)\times \cdots \times(\mathcal X_s-z_{m-m_\mathrm{tor}})\big)/\mathcal B_s\right)
    \end{align*}
    for $(z_1,\dots,z_{m-m_{\mathrm{tor}}})\in \mathcal X_s^{m-m_{\mathrm{tor}}}\simeq p^{-1}(y)\cap \mathcal X_s^m.$
    By Proposition \ref{prop_abel_quotient}, either

\noindent(i) for general $s\in S$,
    \begin{align*}
        \dim \left(\big((\mathcal X_s-z_1)\times \cdots \times(\mathcal X_s-z_{m-m_\mathrm{tor}})\big)/\mathcal B_s\right)\geq \dim \mathcal X_s^{m-m_\mathrm{tor}}-\dim \mathcal B_s+m-m_{\mathrm{tor}}
    \end{align*}
    (ii) or $$\mathrm{Mod}.\dim_{\mathcal G^{[m-m_{\mathrm{tor}}]}/\mathcal B}(S)=\mathrm{Mod}.\dim_{\mathcal G^{[m-m_{\mathrm{tor}}]}}(S)=\dim \iota_S(S).$$ 
    
    Note that case (ii) gives that $$\dim \iota_S(S)=\mathrm{Mod}.\dim_{\mathcal G'/h(\mathcal H)}(S)=\mathrm{Mod}.\dim_{\mathcal G^{[m]}/\mathcal H}(S)$$
    where the first equation is given by the inclusion $\mathcal G^{[m-m_{\mathrm{tor}}]}/\mathcal B\subset \mathcal G'/h(\mathcal H)$ in \eqref{eq_cd_quotient_isogeny}.

    If $m\geq \dim S$, combining with \eqref{eq_torus_fiber_dim} and \eqref{eq_abelian_quot_dim}, we thus conclude the proof in both cases.
<!-- end proof-21 -->
<!-- definition-7: body_md -->
\label{def_adelic_line_bundle} Let $\mathcal U$ be an arithmetic variety.
    An \emph{adelic line bundle} $\overline{\mathcal L}=({\mathcal L},({\mathcal Z}_i,\overline{\mathcal L}_i,\ell_i)_{i\ge1})$ on ${\mathcal U}$ consists of:
\begin{enumerate}
    \item[(1)]a line bundle ${\mathcal L}$ on ${\mathcal U}$, called the underlying line bundle of $\overline{\mathcal L}$,
    \item[(2)]a projective model ${\mathcal Z}_i$ of ${\mathcal U}$ for each $i\ge1$,
    \item[(3)]a $\mathbb{Q}$-hermitian line bundle $\overline{\mathcal L}_i$ on each ${\mathcal Z}_i$, with an isomorphism $\ell_i:{\mathcal L}_i|_{\mathcal U}\simeq \mathcal L$
\end{enumerate}
such that it satisfies the Cauchy condition:
$$-\epsilon_j\overline{\mathcal E}\le\widehat{\mathrm{div}}(\ell_i\ell_j^{-1})\le\epsilon_j\overline{\mathcal E}$$
for some boundary divisor $\overline{\mathcal E}$ of ${\mathcal U}$ and sequence of rational number $(\epsilon_i)_{i\ge1}$ converging to $0$.

Let $\overline {\mathcal L}=({\mathcal L},({\mathcal Z}_i,\overline{\mathcal L}_i,\ell_i)_{i\ge1})$ and $\overline {\mathcal L}'=({\mathcal L}',({\mathcal Z}_i',\overline{\mathcal L}_i',\ell_i')_{i\ge1})$ be two adelic line bundles on $\mathcal U$. We say $\overline{\mathcal L}$ is isomorphic to $\overline{\mathcal L}'$ if there exists an isomorphism $\iota:{\mathcal L}\rightarrow {\mathcal L}'$ such that $\widehat{\mathrm{div}}(\ell_i'^{-1}\iota\ell_i)$ converges to $0$.
<!-- end definition-7 -->
<!-- definition-8: body_md -->
An adelic line bundle $\overline L$ is said to be
\begin{enumerate}
    \item[(1)]\emph{strongly nef} (resp. \emph{semipositive}) if it is a limit of nef (resp. \emph{relatively semipositive}) $\mathbb{Q}$-hermitian line bundles;
    \item[(2)]\emph{nef} if for any strongly nef adelic line bundle $\overline M$ on $U$, $\overline L+\overline M$ is nef;
    \item[(3)]\emph{integrable} if there are strongly nef adelic line bundles $\overline M_1,\overline M_2$ on $U$ such that $\overline L=\overline M_1-\overline M_2$.
\end{enumerate}
Denote by $\widehat{\mathrm{Pic}}(U)_{\mathrm{int}}$ the isomorphism class group of integrable adelic line bundles.
<!-- end definition-8 -->
<!-- lemma-7: body_md -->
\label{lemma_height_ineq_nef_and_big}
    Let $\overline L$ be an adelic line bundle on $U$ such that its restriction on any closed subvariety is nef and big. Then for any integrable adelic line bundle $\overline M$, there exists a constant $\ell>0$ depending on $\overline L$ and $\overline M$, such that $$h_{\overline L}(x)\geq \ell h_{\overline M}(x)$$
    for any $x\in U(\overline{\mathbb{Q}}).$
<!-- end lemma-7 -->
<!-- proof-22: body_md -->
We proceed by induction on $\dim U$. Let $\overline M_1$ and $\overline M_2$ be nef adelic line bundles on $U$ such that $\overline M=\overline M_1-\overline M_2$. Then by \eqref{eq_Siu_inequality}
    \begin{align*}\widehat{\mathrm{vol}}(N\overline L-\overline M)&=\widehat{\mathrm{vol}}(N\overline L+\overline M_2-\overline M_1)\\&=(N+\overline L_1+\overline M_2)^{d+1}-(d+1)((N\overline L_1+\overline M_2)^{d}\cdot \overline M_1)
    \end{align*}
    which is greater than $0$ when $N\gg 0.$ Let $s$ be an effective section of a multiple of $N\overline L-\overline M$. Then $h_{N\overline L-\overline M}(x)>0$ on $(U\setminus\lvert\mathrm{div}(s)\rvert)(\overline{\mathbb{Q}})$. By applying the induction hypothesis to each irreducible component of $\mathrm{div}(s)$, there exists a constant $\ell'$ such that $h_{\overline L}(x)\geq\ell' h_{\overline M}(x)$ on $\lvert\mathrm{div}(s)\rvert(\overline {\mathbb{Q}})$. We then conclude the proof by putting $\ell:=\displaystyle\min\left\{\frac{1}{N},\ell'\right\}$.
<!-- end proof-22 -->
<!-- proposition-10: body_md -->
\label{integrable}
For any symmetric polarization $L$ of ${\mathcal A}$ and its invariant adelic extension $\overline L$, there is a nef adelic line bundle $\overline H$ on $S$ and a positive integer $m$ such that 
$$\mathcal{O}(\overline D_{[0]}^{(i)})+m\overline L+\pi_{\mathcal G/S}^*\overline H \quad(\mathrm{resp.\ }\mathcal{O}(\overline D_{[\infty]}^{(i)})+n\overline L+\pi_{\mathcal G/S}^*\overline H)$$
is nef.
In particular, $\overline D_{[0]}^{(i)}$ and $\overline D_{[\infty]}^{(i)}$ are integrable.
<!-- end proposition-10 -->
<!-- proof-23: body_md -->
We only prove the statement for $\overline D_{[0]}^{(i)}$. The proof for $\overline D_{[\infty]}^{(i)}$ is verbatim.

We only need to consider the toric rank $1$ case. Indeed, let $p_i:\overline{\mathcal G}\to\overline{\mathcal G}_i$ (resp. $p_i:{\mathcal G}\to{\mathcal G}_i$) be the push-forward along the $i$-th projection map $(\mathbb{P}^1)^t\to\mathbb{P}^1$ (resp. $\mathbb{G}_{m}^t\to\mathbb{G}_{m}$). Then ${\mathcal G}_i$ is a semiabelian scheme and $\overline{\mathcal G}_i$ is its compactification. Let $D_{[0]}$ be the divisor on $\overline{\mathcal G}_i$. Then $p_i^*D_{[0]}=D_{[0]}^{(i)}$. Once the statement is true for $\overline D_{[0]}$, then so is it for $\overline D_{[0]}^{(i)}=p_i^*\overline D_{[0]}$. Thus, we may and do assume $t=1$ and omit the superscript $(i)$.

Let ${\mathcal A}^\vee$ be the dual abelian scheme of ${\mathcal A}$ and ${\mathcal P}$ the Poincaré torsor over ${\mathcal A}\times_S{\mathcal A}^\vee$.
Then we have the following properties:
\begin{enumerate}
    \item ${\mathcal P}$ is a biextension of the pair $(\mathcal A,\mathcal A^\vee)$ by $\mathbb G_m$, that is, ${\mathcal P}$ is a semiabelian scheme over ${\mathcal A}^\vee$ with the abelian part $\mathcal A\times_S{\mathcal A}^\vee$, and ${\mathcal P}$ is also a semiabelian scheme over $\mathcal A$ with the abelian part $\mathcal A^\vee\times_S\mathcal A$.
    \item Applying the Weil--Barsotti formula \cite[\S III.18]{Oort1966group} fiberwisely, there is a section $s:S\to{\mathcal A}^\vee$ such that ${\mathcal G}=s^*{\mathcal P}.$
    \item Let $\overline{\mathcal P}=({\mathcal P}\times\mathbb P^1)/\mathbb{G}_m$ be the $\mathbb P^1$-toric compactification of ${\mathcal P}$ such that $\overline{\mathcal G}=s^*\overline {\mathcal P}$. Then the boundary divisors of $\overline{\mathcal G}$ are exactly the pull-back of the boundary divisors of $\overline{\mathcal P}$. Moreover, $\overline{\mathcal P}$ is also the $\mathbb P^1$-toric compactification of ${\mathcal P}$ as a semiabelian scheme over ${\mathcal A}$.
    \item The the fiberwise multiplication by $n$ map $[n]_{{\mathcal P}}$ (resp. $[n^\vee]_{{\mathcal P}}$) of ${\mathcal P}$ over ${\mathcal A}^\vee$ (resp. ${\mathcal A}$), extends uniquely to $\overline{\mathcal P}$. We denote the extension as $[n]_{\overline {\mathcal P}}$ (resp. $[n^\vee]_{\overline {\mathcal P}}$).
\end{enumerate}
To summarize, we have the following commutative diagrams:
\[\begin{tikzcd}
    \overline{\mathcal G} &
	\overline{\mathcal P} && \\
	& & {{\mathcal A}\times_S{\mathcal A}^\vee} & {\mathcal A} \\
	&S & {{\mathcal A}^\vee} & S
    \arrow[from=1-1, to=1-2]
    \arrow["s", from=3-2, to=3-3]
    \arrow["{\pi_{\overline {\mathcal G}/S}}"', curve={height=18pt}, from=1-1, to=3-2]
	\arrow["\pi"', from=1-2, to=2-3]
	\arrow["{\pi_{\overline {\mathcal P}/{\mathcal A}}}", curve={height=-18pt}, from=1-2, to=2-4]
	\arrow["\pi_{\overline {\mathcal P}/{\mathcal A}^\vee}"', curve={height=18pt}, from=1-2, to=3-3]
	\arrow["{p'}", from=2-3, to=2-4]
	\arrow["p"', from=2-3, to=3-3]
	\arrow[from=2-4, to=3-4]
	\arrow[from=3-3, to=3-4]
\end{tikzcd}\]
and 
\begin{equation}\label{cd_multiplication}
    \begin{tikzcd}
    \overline{{\mathcal P}} & \overline{{\mathcal P}} \\
    {{\mathcal A}\times{\mathcal A}^\vee} & {{\mathcal A}\times{\mathcal A}^\vee} \\
    {\mathcal A} & {\mathcal A}
    \arrow["{[n]_{\overline{{\mathcal P}}}}", from=1-1, to=1-2]
    \arrow[from=1-1, to=2-1]
    \arrow[from=1-2, to=2-2]
    \arrow["{[n]_{{\mathcal A}}\times_S \mathrm{id}_{{\mathcal A}^\vee}}"', from=2-1, to=2-2]
    \arrow["{p'}"', from=2-1, to=3-1]
    \arrow["{p'}", from=2-2, to=3-2]
    \arrow["{[n]_{{\mathcal A}}}"', from=3-1, to=3-2]
                                                   
    \arrow["{\pi_{\overline{{\mathcal P}}/{\mathcal A}}}"', curve={height=24pt}, from=1-1, to=3-1]
    \arrow["{\pi_{\overline{{\mathcal P}}/{\mathcal A}}}", curve={height=-24pt}, from=1-2, to=3-2]
\end{tikzcd}
\quad
\begin{tikzcd}
    \overline{{\mathcal P}} & \overline{{\mathcal P}} \\
    {{\mathcal A}\times{\mathcal A}^\vee} & {{\mathcal A}\times{\mathcal A}^\vee} \\
    {\mathcal A}^\vee & {\mathcal A}^\vee
    \arrow["{[n^\vee]_{\overline{{\mathcal P}}}}", from=1-1, to=1-2]
    \arrow[from=1-1, to=2-1]
    \arrow[from=1-2, to=2-2]
    \arrow["{\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal A}\times[n]_{{\mathcal A}^\vee}}"', from=2-1, to=2-2]
    \arrow["{p}"', from=2-1, to=3-1]
    \arrow["{p}", from=2-2, to=3-2]
    \arrow["{[n]_{{\mathcal A}^\vee}}"', from=3-1, to=3-2]
                                                   
    \arrow["{\pi_{\overline{{\mathcal P}}/{\mathcal A}^\vee}}"', curve={height=24pt}, from=1-1, to=3-1]
    \arrow["{\pi_{\overline{{\mathcal P}}/{\mathcal A}^\vee}}", curve={height=-24pt}, from=1-2, to=3-2]
\end{tikzcd}.
\end{equation}
Notice that if the statement of the proposition is true for the boundary divisors of $\overline {\mathcal P}$ over $\mathcal A^\vee$, then it is also true for the boundary divisors of $\overline {\mathcal G}$ over $S$ via pull-backs. Hence we only need to consider the case of $\mathcal P/\mathcal A^\vee$. By abuse of notation, we still use $D_{[0]}$ to denote the boundary divisor on $\overline {\mathcal P}$.


From the property \textnormal{(3)} and \textnormal{(4)}, we can see that
$$[n]_{\overline{\mathcal P}}^*D_{[0]}=[n^\vee]_{\overline{\mathcal P}}^*D_{[0]}=nD_{[0]}.$$

Let $L'$ be a symmetric polarization of ${\mathcal A}^\vee$ and $\overline L'$ its invariant adelic extension. Since $p'^*L+p^*L'$ is relatively ample over $S$ and $D_{[0]}$ is relatively ample over ${\mathcal A}\times_S{\mathcal A}^\vee$, we can take an integer $m$ large enough such that the line bundle
$$N=\mathcal{O}(D_{[0]})+m(\pi_{\overline {\mathcal P}/{\mathcal A}}^*L+\pi_{\overline {\mathcal P}/{\mathcal A}^\vee}^*L')$$
on $\overline{\mathcal P}$ is relatively ample over $S$ (see \cite[Proposition 13.65]{GortzWedhorn}).

We claim that $(\overline{\mathcal P},[2]_{\overline{\mathcal P}}\circ[2^\vee]_{\overline{\mathcal P}},N)$ is a polarized dynamical system over $S$. By the commutative diagram \eqref{cd_multiplication}, we have the isomorphism \begin{equation*}\label{eq_inv_dsh}
    \begin{aligned}
([2]_{\overline{{\mathcal P}}}\circ[2^\vee]_{\overline{{\mathcal P}}})^* N
&= [2^\vee]_{\overline{{\mathcal P}}}^*\,[2]_{\overline{{\mathcal P}}}^*\Bigl(\mathcal{O}(D_{[0]}) + m\pi_{\overline{{\mathcal P}}/{\mathcal A}}^*L + m\pi_{\overline{{\mathcal P}}/{\mathcal A}^\vee}^*L'\Bigr)\\
&= \mathcal{O}(4D_{[0]}) + m\,\pi_{\overline{{\mathcal P}}/{\mathcal A}}^*[2]_{{\mathcal A}}^*L + m\,\pi_{\overline{{\mathcal P}}/{\mathcal A}^\vee}^*[2^\vee]_{{\mathcal A}^\vee}^*L'=4N.
\end{aligned}
\end{equation*}Therefore, there exists a unique nef invariant adelic extension $\overline  N$ of $N$. Since $\overline N-m(\pi_{\overline {\mathcal P}/{\mathcal A}^\vee}^*\overline  L+\pi_{\overline {\mathcal P}/{\mathcal A}}^*\overline L')$ is an invariant extension of $D_{[0]}$, by the uniqueness we obtain $\overline D_{[0]}=\overline N-m(\pi_{\overline {\mathcal P}/{\mathcal A}^\vee}^*\overline  L+\pi_{\overline {\mathcal P}/{\mathcal A}}^*\overline L')$, which is integrable.
<!-- end proof-23 -->
<!-- remark-5: body_md -->
The nef line bundle $\overline H$ in the proposition can be taken to be the pull-back of $m\overline L'$ via the section $s:S\rightarrow \mathcal A^\vee$.
<!-- end remark-5 -->
<!-- proposition-11: body_md -->
\label{prop_dsh_toric_betti}
Let $g_{[0]}^{(i)}$ (resp. $g_{[\infty]}^{(i)}$) be the Green function of $\overline D_{[0]}^{(i)}$ (resp. $\overline D_{[\infty]}^{(i)}$) on ${\mathcal G}(\mathbb{C})$ and $\widetilde{g}_{[0]}^{(i)}$ (resp. $\widetilde{g}_{[\infty]}^{(i)}$) its pull-back to ${\mathcal G}_{\widetilde S}$. Then
$$\widetilde{g}_{[0]}^{(i)}(\cdot)=\max\{-\log|b_{\mathrm{tor},i}(\cdot))|,0\}\quad(\mathrm{resp.\ }\widetilde{g}_{[\infty]}^{(i)}(\cdot)=\max\{\log|b_{\mathrm{tor},i}(\cdot))|,0\}).$$
In particular, the toric Betti currents $\widetilde \omega_{\mathrm{tor},i}$ descend to currents $\omega_{\mathrm{tor},i}$ on $\mathcal G$, which are differences of semipositive $(1,1)$-currents.
<!-- end proposition-11 -->
<!-- proof-24: body_md -->
We may assume $t=1$ and only deal with $\widetilde g_{[0]}$. Let
$$f(x)=\widetilde{g}_{[0]}(x)-\max\{-\log|b_{\mathrm{tor}}(x)|,0\}$$
be the difference. 

Since $b_{\mathrm{tor}}$ is a group homomorphism and $[n]^*\overline D_{[0]}=n\overline D_{[0]}$, we have $f(nx)=nf(x)$. In fact, it suffices to prove $f=0$ on $(\mathbb{G}_{m})_{\widetilde{S}}\subset{\mathcal G}_{\widetilde{S}}$. Indeed, this implies $f(x)=0$ for those $x\in{\mathcal G}_{\widetilde{S}}$ satisfying $nx\in(\mathbb{G}_{m})_{\widetilde{S}}$ for some positive integer $n$. Such points $x$ are dense in the analytic topology in ${\mathcal G}_{\widetilde{S}}$. The continuity of $f$ concludes the proof. The restriction $b_{\mathrm{tor}}|_{(\mathbb G_m)_{\widetilde S}}$ is just the projection $(\mathbb G_m)_{\widetilde S}(\mathbb{C})=\widetilde S(\mathbb{C})\times\mathbb{C}^\times\to\mathbb{C}^\times.$ 

On the other hand, the Zariski closure of $\mathbb{G}_{m,S}$ in $\overline {\mathcal G}$ is exactly $\mathbb P^1_S.$ Moreover, by the uniqueness of the invariant adelic line bundle, the restriction of $\overline D_{[0]}$ on it is nothing but the pull-back of $(D_{[0],{\mathbb Z}},\max\{-\log\lvert\cdot\rvert,0\})$ via $\mathbb P_S^1\rightarrow \mathbb P^1_\mathbb{Z}.$ This concludes the proof for the first assertion.

For the second assertion, $\omega_{\mathrm{tor}}$ descends to the current $dd^c (g_{[0]}+g_{[\infty]})$ by the definition. We thus conclude the proof by the integrability of $g_{[0]}+g_{[\infty]}.$
<!-- end proof-24 -->
<!-- lemma-8: body_md -->
\label{lemm_fubini}
Let $M$ be a complex manifold of dimension $d$. Let $N$ be a real manifold of dimension $2r$. Let $(p,q):M\to N\times\mathbb{C}^{d-r}$ be a real-analytic local diffeomorphism such that for any $x\in N$, $p^{-1}(x)$ is complex analytic and $q|_{p^{-1}(x)}:p^{-1}(x)\to\mathbb{C}^{d-r}$ is holomorphic. Let $\alpha$ be a smooth $2r$-form on $N$ such that $p^*\alpha$ is semi-positive on $M$. Let $g$ be a continuous dsh function on $M$. Denote by $\beta=(dd^cg)^{d-r}$ the current on $M$. Then for any continuous function $f$ with compact support on $M$,
$$(x\in N)\mapsto\int_{p^{-1}(x)}f\beta|_{p^{-1}(x)}$$
is a continuous function with compact support, and
$$\int_Mf\beta\wedge p^*\alpha=\int_N\Big(\int_{p^{-1}(x)}f\beta|_{p^{-1}(x)}\Big)\alpha.$$
<!-- end lemma-8 -->
<!-- proof-25: body_md -->
Take a uniform approximation $(g_m)_{m\ge1}$ of $g$ by smooth dsh functions on the support of $f$. Denote $\beta_m=(dd^cg_m)^{d-r}$. By definition
$$\int_Mf\beta\wedge p^*\alpha=\lim_{m\to\infty}\int_Mf\beta_m\wedge p^*\alpha,$$
and
$$\int_{p^{-1}(x)}f\beta|_{p^{-1}(x)}=\lim_{m\to\infty}\int_{p^{-1}(x)}f\beta_m|_{p^{-1}(x)}.$$
By the Fubini theorem for smooth forms, $\displaystyle\int_{p^{-1}(x)}f\beta_m|_{p^{-1}(x)}$ is continuous in $x$ and
$$\int_Mf\beta_m\wedge p^*\alpha=\int_N\Big(\int_{p^{-1}(x)}f\beta_m|_{p^{-1}(x)}\Big)\alpha.$$
